"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
夏尔城堡惊魂<BR>
独幕剧<BR>
巴罗斯·库尔　著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
出场人物<BR>
克拉维德斯，帝国卫队的队长，西罗帝尔人。<BR>
阿娜拉，一名丹莫女仆。<BR>
乌利斯，帝国卫队的一名副官，阿尔贡。<BR>
佐拉萨，一名年轻的阿尔贡法师。<BR>
<BR>
深夜。剧幕于斯卡斯·阿努德的一座城堡的宏伟入口大厅内拉开，这里满是华美的家具和挂毯。火把是唯一的光源。大厅中央的巨大铁门便是通往城堡的主入口，通往上层的楼梯坐落其侧。舞台的左侧是一扇通往图书馆的门，目前是关闭着的。舞台的右侧是一副足有二十尺高的巨大护甲，几乎触及到天花板。虽然空无一人，但可以听见一个女人的歌声从图书馆的门里传出来。<BR>
<BR>
敲打铁前门的一声巨响打断了女人的歌声。图书馆的门打开了，一个相貌普通的女仆阿娜拉匆匆跑出来打开了前门。身着帝国制服的英俊男子，克拉维德斯站在那里。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：晚安，先生。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：晚安。你的主人在家吗？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：不，先生，只有我在这里。我的主人瑟杜拉·科纳·泰瓦尼·霍达夫·夏尔在他的避暑庄园。有什么我可以为您效劳的吗？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：或许吧。我可以进来吗？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：当然可以，先生。请进。我能为您端上一杯飞令酒吗？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯走进大厅并环顾四周。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：不，谢谢。你叫什么名字？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：阿娜拉，先生。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：阿娜拉，你的主人什么时候离开了斯卡斯·阿努德？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：超过两个星期以前。这就是为什么只有我在这个城堡里，先生。所有其他的仆人和奴隶都跟着主人一起走了。有什么问题吗？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：是的。你认识一位名叫苏尔·哈瑞发的灰烬民吗？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：不，先生。我并不认识这个人。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：你大概也没有这个机会了。他已经死了。在数小时前，他被发现在灰烬因冻伤而死。他当时有些狂乱，话语乱到无法理解，但在他最后的话语中出现了“城堡”和“夏尔”两个词。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：死于冻伤？在灰烬的夏天？天哪，这太奇怪了。我想我的主人可能会认识这个人，但鉴于他是一个灰烬民，而我的主人出身泰瓦尼家族，请恕我无礼，先生，我不认为他们会是朋友。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：那是你主人的图书馆？我能进去看看吗？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：请随意，先生。我们没有什么好隐瞒的。我们是忠诚的帝国人民。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：我听说所有泰瓦尼家族的人都如此。<BR>
<BR>
（剧作家的注释：这句话应不带任何讽刺意味地说出。观众一定会发笑——从未失效，不管当地人的政见为何。）<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯进入图书馆，并仔细查看书籍。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：图书馆需要打扫了。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：是的，先生，在您敲门的时候我正在打扫。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：我对此很感谢。如果你已经打扫完了，我就不会注意到这片灰尘中有一处空白，想必一本相当大的书最近被拿走了。看起来你的主人似乎是一名法师。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：不，先生。我的意思是，他在这方面做了很多研究，但他从未施放过任何法术，如果你所指的法师是这样的话。他是一位学者，去过学院和各种地方。喔，现在我想起来了，我知道这本书怎么回事了。来自学院的一位学者昨天到过这里，并借走了几本书。他是主人的一位朋友，所以我想应该没什么问题。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：这位学者，他是不是叫做沃维姆？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：好像是，我不太记得了。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：昨晚，我们在学院拘捕了一位名叫科玛·沃维姆的亡灵法师，他涉嫌此案。我们不知道他在学院都做些什么，但肯定是一些非法的事情。是那位学者借的书吗？一个瘦小的，拖着残腿的跛脚之人？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：不，先生，这不是昨天来的那位学者。他是个步伐稳健的大个子，所以我留心了一下。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：我要去查看一下这个房子的其他部分，如果不介意的话。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯上了楼，并在二楼楼梯和上面的房间里说出接下来的台词。阿娜拉继续在楼下打扫，把一个高椅背的椅子移到护甲前，以便清洗地板。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：我能问一下吗，先生，您在找些什么？也许我可以帮您。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：这些就是城堡的全部房间了吗？没有任何密道？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉（笑）：噢，先生，瑟杜拉·科纳·泰瓦尼·霍达夫·夏尔要密道做什么？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯（看着那副护甲）：你的主人身材很魁梧。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉（笑）：噢，先生，不要说笑了。那只是用来装饰的巨人护甲。我的主人在十年前杀了那个巨人，然后把它留下来作为纪念。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：没错，我记得我刚来这里履职的时候听说过这件事。是个姓夏尔的人杀死了巨人，但我不认为他的名字是霍达夫。可能记忆模糊了。那个巨人的名字是？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：我恐怕我不记得了，先生。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：我记得。他叫托尔范。“我从托尔范的盾里出来”。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：我不明白，先生。托尔范的盾？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯抛下楼梯，仔细查看那副护甲。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：苏尔·哈瑞发说了一些关于从托尔范的盾里出来的话。当时我以为他是语无伦次，胡言乱语的。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：但是他没有盾牌，先生。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯把高椅背的椅子推开，护甲下露出一面固定着的巨大盾牌。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：是的，他有。被你用椅子挡住了。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：我并不是故意这么做的，先生！我只是在打扫！我每天都看见这副护甲，先生，我发誓我从未发现过这个盾牌！<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：没事的，阿娜拉，我相信你。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯推动盾牌，盾牌向后退去，露出了一个地道。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：看来瑟杜拉·科纳·泰瓦尼·霍达夫·夏尔的确需要一个密道。你能给我一支火把吗？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：天哪，我从来没见过这个！<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉从墙上取下一支火把，并递给克拉维德斯。克拉维德斯进入地道。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：在这等着。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉看着克拉维德斯走下地道，消失在视野中。她显得很焦虑，并最后跑向前门。当她打开大门时，乌利斯，一名帝国卫队的阿尔贡副官站在入口处。她尖叫起来。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：我很抱歉吓到你了。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：现在不是时候！走开！<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：恐怕队长不这样想，小姐。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：你是……和队长一起的？天啊。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯脸色苍白地走出地道。他花了一会儿工夫才开口说话。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：队长？底下有些什么？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯（对阿娜拉）：你知不知道你的主人是个亡灵法师？而且你们的地窖里塞满了尸体？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉昏倒了。乌利斯将她抱到椅子上并扶她躺下。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：让我看看，先生。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：你待会能看个够。我们现在需要驻地内的每个士兵过来搬走全部的尸体。乌利斯，我见过的战场已经够多了，但从来没见过哪次像今天这样。没有两具尸体是相似的。凯季特人，斯洛德，丹莫，西罗帝尔人，布莱顿人，诺德人，活活烧死的，毒死的，电死的，溶解的，身体被撕裂的，内脏被挖出来的，被撕成碎片再缝起来的。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：你认为那个灰烬民从这里逃了出来，这就是真相？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：我不知道。为什么会有人做这样的事，乌利斯？<BR>
<BR>
有人敲门。克拉维德斯前去应门。一名年轻的阿尔贡女子，佐拉萨站在门口，拿着一个包裹和一封信。<BR>
<BR>
佐拉萨：早安，你不是夏尔领主，对吧？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：不是。你拿着什么？<BR>
<BR>
佐拉萨：一封信和一个包裹，我应该要交给他。他很快就会回来吗？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：我不这么认为。谁给你这个包裹的？<BR>
<BR>
佐拉萨：我在学院的老师，科玛·沃维姆。他行动不便，所以他要我帮他带这些给阁下。实际上，说实话，我应该在昨天晚上就交给他，不过我太忙了。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：你好，姐妹。等我们碰到阁下时，我们会转交给他。<BR>
<BR>
佐拉萨：噢，你好，兄弟。我早就听说在斯卡斯·阿努德有一位英俊的阿尔贡。不好意思，我答应过科玛·沃维姆要亲手将包裹直接交到阁下手里。我已经晚了，我不能再……<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：我们是帝国卫兵，小姐。我们会拿走这个包裹和信件。<BR>
<BR>
佐拉萨有些不情愿地将信件和包裹交给克拉维德斯。她转身离去。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：你会在学院里吗，如果我们需要见你的话？<BR>
<BR>
佐拉萨：是的。祝你好运，兄弟。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：再见，姐妹。<BR>
<BR>
在佐拉萨离开后，克拉维德斯打开包裹。里面是一本夹着许多活页的书。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：看来我们已经找到了那本失踪的书。恰好送到我们手中。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯开始默默地阅读这本书。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯（自言自语，非常开心）：另一个在斯卡斯·阿努德的阿尔贡！而且那么漂亮。我希望我们刚才对她不会太失礼。我已经厌倦了这些皮肤光滑又湿润的女人了，如果能够在不当值的时候碰面就太美妙了。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯说着，一边拆开信件阅读。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯（继续自言自语）：她看起来像是和我一样从南方来的。你知道，那些来自黑沼泽北部的阿尔贡都……很……<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯继续看信，被信里的内容吓得瞠目结舌。克拉维德斯跳到了书的最后，开始读最后的几句话。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯（朗读）：用黑色墨水写着，“男性凯季特人显示了出人意料的极弱的闪电抗性，即使是对一个简单的闪电法术，但在持续数天对其施放一个中级的酸性法术后，得到了一个有趣的生理学结果”用红色墨水在空白处写着，“是的，我看到了。这个酸性法术是均匀地施放在整个身体上吗？”用黑色墨水写着，“女性诺德人可忍受十六个小时的寒霜法术，最终以假死的状态将她冻结，并以这个状态逐渐死亡。男性诺德和灰烬民都不会如此，他们陷入昏迷的时间要早得多，但随后会醒过来。那个灰烬民试图逃跑，但我阻止了他。那个诺德人接着对一个简单的火焰法术产生了有趣的化学过度反应，然后就死了。见附随的图解”用红色墨水写着，“是，我见着了。烧伤的痕迹和身体损伤的模样令人想起某种内部焚化，可能是短时间的火烧和长时间的冰冻一起作用的结果。很遗憾我无法亲自来观察这个实验，但我非常欣赏你周密的实验记录”用黑色墨水写着，“感谢你关于对我的女仆阿娜拉逐渐缓慢下毒的建议。你所建议的计量产生了极好的效果，巧妙地腐蚀着她的记忆。我打算逐渐地增加毒性，看看何时她才会后知后觉。说到这，对于还没有得到任何阿尔贡实验体，我觉得很可惜，不过奴隶贩子向我保证会在秋天送来一些健康的样本。我希望测试他们的新陈代谢情况，并与精灵和人类的进行比较。我的理论是，一个中级等幅波的闪电法术在阿尔贡身上不会导致他在至少几个小时之内死亡，类似于我在女性西罗帝尔人，以及，当然了，巨人身上获得的结果”用红色墨水写着，“要等到秋天才能看到真是太可惜了”。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯（朗读信件）：用红色墨水，“这是你要的阿尔贡。请让我知道实验结果”署名为“科玛·沃维姆”。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：吉娜瑞斯啊，这不是亡灵法术。这是毁灭系法术。科玛·沃维姆和科纳·泰瓦尼·霍达夫·夏尔不是在对死亡进行实验，而是在研究法术折磨的极限。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：这封信的收信人不是科纳·泰瓦尼·霍达夫·夏尔，而是瑟杜拉·亚奇拉·夏尔。他的妻子，你认为呢？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：亚奇拉。我听说那就是杀死巨人的泰瓦尼家族成员。我们最好带那位女仆离开这里。她需要一位治疗者。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯叫醒阿娜拉。她看起来有些混乱。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：发生了什么事？你们是谁？<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：别担心，一切都会没事的。我们要带你去找治疗者。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：你需要外套吗，亚奇拉？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉：谢谢，不了，我不冷——<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉/亚奇拉停顿了，意识到自己被设了圈套。克拉维德斯和乌利斯拔出了他们的剑。<BR>
<BR>
克拉维德斯：您的手指上还有黑色墨水，尊贵的夫人。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：而且当你在门口看到我时，你还以为我是你朋友沃维姆送来的阿尔贡。这就是为什么你会说，“现在不是时候，走开”。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜拉/亚奇拉：你们比阿娜拉机灵多了。她从来都不明白到底发生了什么事，甚至在我将法术毒性加剧了三倍，使她痛苦致死，也浑然不觉。<BR>
<BR>
乌利斯：你原本打算对我做什么，闪电还是火焰？<BR>
<BR>
阿娜娜/亚奇拉：闪电。我发现火焰的效果太难预测了。<BR>
<BR>
在她说话时，火把上的火焰熄灭了。舞台陷入彻底的黑暗。<BR>
<BR>
从中传出打斗的声音，剑撞击的铿锵之声。突然，一道闪电一闪而过，随后便安静了。在黑暗之中，阿娜娜/亚奇拉说话了。<BR>
<BR>
阿娜娜/亚奇拉：太美妙了。<BR>
<BR>
随着布幕的缓缓拉阖，多道闪电不断划过。<BR>
<BR>
剧终<BR>
<BR>

> BOOK.FNAM bookskill_destruction2
Response to Bero's Speech
《对贝罗演讲的回应》

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Response to Bero's Speech<BR>
by Malviser, Battlemage<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
On the 14th of Last Seed, an illusionist by the name of Berevar Bero gave a very ignorant speech at the Chantry of Julianos in the Imperial City.  As ignorant speeches are hardly uncommon, there was no reason to respond to it.  Unfortunately, he has since had the speech privately printed as "Bero's Speech to the Battlemages," and it's received some small, undeserved attention in academic circles.  Let us put his misconceptions to rest.<BR>
<BR>
Bero began his lecture with an occasionally factual account of famous Battlemages from Zurin Arctus, Tiber Septim's Imperial Battlemage, to Jagar Tharn, Uriel Septim VII's Imperial Battlemage.  His intent was to show that where it matters, the Battlemage relies on other Schools of Magicka, not the School of Destruction which is supposedly a Battlemage's particular forte.  Allow me first to dispute these so-called historical facts.<BR>
<BR>
Zurin Arctus did not create the golem Numidium by spells of  Mysticism and Conjuration as Bero alleges.  The truth is that we don't know how Numidium was created or if it was a golem or atronach in any traditional sense of those words.  Uriel V's Battlemage Hethoth was not an Imperial Battlemage -- he was simply a sorcerer in the employ of the Empire, thus which spells he cast in the various battles on Akavir are irrelevant, not to mention heresay.  Bero calls Empress Morihatha's Battlemage Welloc "an accomplished diplomat" but not "a powerful student of the School of Destruction."  I congratulate Bero on correctly identifying an Imperial Battlemage, but there are many written examples of Welloc's skill in the School of Destruction.  The sage Celarus, for example, wrote extensively about Welloc casting the Vampiric Cloud on the rebellious army of Blackrose, causing their strength and skill to pass on to their opponents.  What is this, but an impressive example of the School of Destruction?<BR>
<BR>
Bero rather pathetically includes Jagar Tharn in his list of underachieving Battlemages.  To use an insane traitor as example of rational behavior is an untenable position.  What would Bero prefer?  That Tharn used the School of Destruction to destroy Tamriel by a more traditional means?<BR>
<BR>
Bero uses his misrepresentation of history as the basis for his argument.  Even if he had found four excellent examples from history of Battlemages casting spells outside their School -- and he didn't --  he would only have anecdotal evidence, which isn't enough to support an argument.  I could easily find four examples of illusionists casting healing spells, or nightblades teleporting.  There is a time and a place for everything.<BR>
<BR>
Bero's argument, built on this shaky ground, is that the School of Destruction is not a true school.  He calls it "narrow and shallow" as an avenue of study, and its students impatient, with megalomaniac tendencies.  How can one respond to this?  Someone who knows nothing about casting a spell of Destruction criticizing the School for being too simple?  Summarizing the School of Destruction as learning how to do the "maximum amount of damage in the minimum amount of time" is clearly absurd, and he expounds on his ignorance by listing all the complicated factors studied in his own School of Illusion.<BR>
<BR>
Allow me in response to list the factors studied in the School of Destruction.  The means of delivering the spell matters more in the School of Destruction than any other school, whether it is cast at a touch, at a range, in concentric circles, or cast once to be triggered later.  What forces must be reigned in to cast the spell: fire, lightning, or frost? And what are the advantages and dangers of each?  What are the responses from different targets from the assault of different spells of destruction?  What are the possible defenses and how may they be assailed?  What environmental factors must be taken into consideration?  What are the advantages of a spell of delayed damage?  Bero suggests that the School of Destruction cannot be subtle, yet he forgets about all the Curses that fall under the mantle of the school, sometimes affecting generation after generation in subtle yet sublime ways.<BR>
<BR>
The School of Alteration is a distinct and separate entity from the School of Destruction, and Bero's argument that they should be merged into one is patently ludicrous.  He insists -- again, a man who knows nothing about the Schools of Alteration and Destruction, is the one insisting this -- that "damage" is part of the changing of reality dealt with by the spells of Alteration.  The implication is that Levitation, to list a spell of Alteration, is a close cousin of Shock Bolt, a spell of Destruction.  It would make as much sense to say that the School of Alteration, being all about the actuality of change, should absorb the School of Illusion, being all about the appearance of change.<BR>
<BR>
It certainly isn't a coincidence that a master of the School of Illusion cast this attack on the School of Destruction.  Illusion is, after all, all about masking the truth.<BR>
<BR>
"""
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
对贝罗演讲的回应<BR>
战斗法师，马维泽　著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
在末种月第14日，一个叫做贝热瓦·贝罗的幻术师在帝都的尤利安诺斯教团发表了一次非常无知的演讲。因为无知的演讲屡见不鲜，本并不需要做出回应。不幸的是，他私下将讲演印刷成“贝罗对战斗法师的演讲”，并且还在学术界获得了一些小范围的，不应该获得的注意。让我们终结他的错误想法吧。<BR>
<BR>
贝罗以对包括祖林·阿克图斯这位泰伯·塞普汀的皇家战斗法师，以至于杰迦尔·萨恩——尤利尔·塞普汀七世的帝国法师在内的著名战斗法师们的偶然事件的描述作为他讲演的开始。他的意图是想说明当需要时，战斗法师会依靠其他系别的魔法，而不是本应作为战斗法师特殊专长的毁灭系法术。首先请允许我对这些所谓的史实提出质疑。<BR>
<BR>
祖林·阿克图斯并不像贝罗宣称的那样用神秘系法术和召唤系法术创造出了纳米迪安傀儡。真相是，在对那些词语的传统判断标准下，我们并不知道纳米迪安是怎么产生的，甚至不知道它是不是一个傀儡或者是不是一个元素人。尤利尔五世的所谓战斗法师海瑟斯，严格来说并不是一名皇家战斗法师——他仅仅是一个受雇于帝国的术士，因此他在阿卡维尔的各种战场上施放的是哪种法术就无关紧要了，更不必说那些谣言了。贝罗把莫里哈萨女皇的战斗法师维洛克称作“一位有造诣的外交官”而不是“一位毁灭系的优秀学生”。我首先祝贺贝罗终于能正确的辨别出一位皇家战斗法师，然而有不少书面的例子证实了维洛克的毁灭系技艺。例如，贤者切拉鲁斯，大篇阐述了关于维洛克对黑玫瑰的叛军施放吸收之云，导致他们的力量和技能被传递给他们对手的事迹。这是什么，难道不是一个令人印象深刻的毁灭系例子吗？<BR>
<BR>
贝罗颇为乏味的在他列出的技艺欠佳战斗法师名单中涵盖了杰迦尔·萨恩。将一个发疯的叛徒作为理性行为的范例，这样的立场是站不住脚的。贝罗想要怎么样？让杰迦尔通过更传统的途径使用毁灭系法术来毁灭泰姆瑞尔吗？<BR>
<BR>
贝罗用他对历史的歪曲作为他论点的基础。即使他真的已经找到了四个历史中战斗法师施放其他系法术的极佳例子——事实上他没有——他只有一些道听涂说的证据，这不足以支撑一个论点。我可以轻易找到四个幻术师施放治疗法术，或者夜刃传送的例子。任何事都取决于特定的情况和位置。<BR>
<BR>
贝罗那建立在脆弱基础之上的论据，宣称毁灭系不是一个真正的派系。他称它“短浅”不足以作为学科的一门分支，认为它的学生们没有耐心，并且有自负倾向。这要如何做出回应？一个对施放毁灭系法术一无所知的人批判该系太过简单？把毁灭系总结为学习如何在“最短时间内造成最大伤害”显然是荒谬的，并且他通过他自己的幻术系研究罗列出的所有复杂因素更加加深了他的不学无术。<BR>
<BR>
作为回应请允许我罗列出毁灭系研究出的因素。在毁灭系中释放法术的方法要比在其他任何系中更加重要，不管是近距离施法，远距离施法，范围法术，还是触发型法术都是如此。必须支配哪种力量来施放法术：火焰、闪电，还是寒霜？每一种的优势和威胁是什么？不同目标对不同毁灭系法术袭击的反应如何？可能遭遇到的防御措施有哪些？它们如何被击破？必须考虑什么环境因素？延时伤害性法术的优点是什么？贝罗暗示说毁灭系法术不够隐蔽，但是他忘记了所有受到该系法术侵蚀的那些祸害，有时能以隐蔽至极端的方法影响一代又一代。<BR>
<BR>
变换系不同于毁灭系，是一个独特且有区别的实体，贝罗认为他们应该被并为一系的论点显然是荒唐的。他又一次主张——一个对变换系和毁灭系一无所知的人，这样“主张”--“伤害”属于被变换系法术作用使现实出现的变化中的一部分。言外之意则是说浮空术这个变换系法术是毁灭系法术雷暴术的近亲。这就和声明关于改变现实的变换系，应该向关于改变表像的幻术系学习一样。<BR>
<BR>
一位幻术系大师对毁灭系进行这种抨击肯定不是一个巧合。毕竟，幻术，就是用来掩盖真相的嘛。<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
A Hypothetical Treachery<BR>
A One Act Play<BR>
by Anthil Morvir<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Dramatis Personae<BR>
Malvasian: A High Elf battlemage<BR>
Inzoliah:  A Dark Elf battlemage<BR>
Dolcettus: A Cyrodiil healer<BR>
Schiavas: An Argonian barbarian <BR>
A Ghost<BR>
Some bandits<BR>
<BR>
Scene: Eldenwood<BR>
<BR>
As the curtain rises, we see the misty labyrinthian landscape of the legendary Eldengrove of Valenwood.  All around we hear wolves howling.  A bloodied reptilian figure, SCHIAVAS, breaks through the branches of one of the trees and surveys the area.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: It's clear.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH, a beautiful Dark Elf mage, climbs down from the tree, helped by the barbarian.  There is the sound of footsteps nearby.  Schiavas readies his sword and Inzoliah prepares to cast a spell.  Nothing comes out.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: You're bleeding.  You should have Dolcettus heal that for you.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: He's still drained from all the spells he had to cast down in the caves.  I'm fine.  If we get out of this and no one needs it more, I'll take the last potion of healing.  Where's Malvasian?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN, a High Elf battlemage, and DOLCETTUS, a Cyrodiil healer, emerge from the tree, carrying a heavy chest between the two of them.  They awkwardly try to get down from the tree, carrying their loot.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Here I am, though why I'm carrying the heavy load is beyond me.  I always thought that the advantage of dungeon delving with a great barbarian was that he carried all the loot.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: If I carried that, my hands would be too full to fight.  And tell me if I'm wrong, but not one of the three of you has enough magicka reserved to make it out of here alive.  Not after you electrified and blasted all those homunculuses down below ground.<BR>
<BR>
DOLCETTUS: Homunculi.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: Don't worry, I'm not going to do what you think I'm going to do.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH (innocently): What's that?<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: Kill you all and take the Ebony Mail for myself.  Admit it -- you thought I had that in mind.<BR>
<BR>
DOLCETTUS: What a perfectly horrible thought.  I never thought anyone, no matter how vile and degenerate --<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Why not?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  He needs porters, like he said.  He can't carry the chest and fight off the inhabitants of Eldengrove both.<BR>
<BR>
DOLCETTUS: By Stendarr, of all the mean, conniving, typically Argonian --<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH:  And why do you need me alive?<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: I don't necessarily.  Except that you're prettier than the other two, for a smoothskin that is.  And if something comes after us, it might go for you first.<BR>
<BR>
There is a noise in some bushes nearby.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS: Go check that out.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH:  It's probably a wolf.  These woods are filled with them.  You check it out.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS:  You have a choice, Inzoliah.  Go and you might live.  Stay here, and you definitely won't.<BR>
<BR>
Inzoliah considers and then goes to the bushes.<BR>
<BR>
SCHIAVAS (to Malvasian and Dolcettus): The king of Silvenar will pay good money for the Mail, and we can divide it more nicely between three than four.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: You're so right.<BR>
<BR>
Inzoliah suddenly levitates up to the top of the stage.  A semi-transparent Ghost appears from the bush and rushes at the next person, who happens to be Schiavas.  As the barbarian screams and thrashes at it with his sword, it levels blasts of whirling gas at him.  He crumbles to the ground.  It turns next to Dolcettus, the healer, and as the Ghost focuses its feasting chill on the hapless Dolcettus, Malvasian casts a ball of flame at it that causes it to vaporize into the misty air.<BR>
<BR>
Inzoliah floats back down to the ground as Malvasian examines the bodies of Dolcettus and Schiavas, who are both white-faced from the draining power of the ghost.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: You had some magicka reserved after all.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: So did you.  Are they dead?<BR>
<BR>
Malvasian takes the potion of healing from Dolcettus's pack.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  Yes.  Fortunately, the potion of healing wasn't broken when he fell.  Well, I guess this leaves just the two of us to collect the reward.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: We can't get out of this place without each other.  Like it or not.<BR>
<BR>
The two battlemages pick up the chest and begin plodding carefully through the undergrowth, pausing from time to time at the sound of footsteps or other eerie noises.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Let me make sure I understand.  You have a little bit of magicka left, so you elected to use it to make Schiavas the ghost's target, forcing me to use most of my limited reserve to destroy the creature so I wouldn't be more powerful than you.  That's first-rate thinking.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Thank you.  It's only logical.  Do you have enough power to cast any other spells?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  Naturally.  An experienced battlemage always knows a few minor but highly effective spells for just such a trial.  I take it you, too, have a few tricks up your sleeve?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH:  Of course, like you said.<BR>
<BR>
They pause for a moment before continuing as a fearful wail pierces the air.  When it dies away, they slowly trudge on.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Just as an intellectual exercise, I wonder what spell you would cast at me if we made it out of here without any more combat.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: I hope you're not implying that I would dream of killing you so I would keep the treasure all to myself.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Of course not, nor would I do that to you.  It is merely an intellectual exercise.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Well, in that case, purely as an intellectual exercise, I would probably cast a leech spell on you, to take away your life force and heal myself.  After all, there are brigands on the road between here and Silvenar, and a wounded battlemage with a valuable artifact would make a tempting target.  I'd hate to survive Eldengrove merely to die in the open.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: That's a well-reasoned response.  As for myself, again, not saying I would ever do this, but I think a simple, sudden electrical bolt would serve my purposes admirably.  I agree about the danger of brigands, but don't forget, we also have a potion of healing.  I could easily slay you and heal myself to full capacity.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Very true.  It would end up a question then of whose spell was more effective at that instant.  If our spells counteracted one another and I leeched your life energy only to be crippled by your lightning bolt, then we could both be killed.  Or so near death that a mere potion of healing would scarcely help either one of us, let alone both.  How ironic it would be if two scheming battlemages, not saying we are scheming but for the purpose of this intellectual exercise, were left on the brink of death, completely drained of magicka, with one healing potion to choose from.  Who would get it then?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Logically, whoever drank it first, which in this case would be you since you're holding it.  Now, what if one of us were injured, but not killed?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: Logic would dictate that a scheming battlemage would take the potion, leaving the injured party to the mercy of the elements, I suppose.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: That does seem most sensible.  But suppose that the battlemages, while certainly scheming types, had a certain respect for one another.  Perhaps in that case, the victorious one might, for instance, put the potion up a tree near his or her gravely wounded victim.  Then when the wounded party had enough magicka replenished, he or she would be able to levitate to the tree branches and recover the potion.  By that time, the victorious battlemage would have already collected the reward.<BR>
<BR>
They pause for a moment at the sound of something in the bushes nearby.  Carefully, they climb across the branches of a tree to bypass it.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: I understand what you're saying, but it seems out of character for our hypothetic scheming battlemage to allow his or her victim to live.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: Perhaps.  But it's been my observation that most scheming battlemages enjoy the feeling of having bested someone in combat, and having that person alive to live with the humiliation.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: These hypothetical scheming battlemages sound ... (excitedly) Daylight!  Do you see it?<BR>
<BR>
The two scurry across the branch dropping behind a bush, so we can no longer see them.  We can, however, see the shimmering halo of sunlight.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN (behind the tall bush): We made it.<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH (likewise, behind the tall bush): Indeed.<BR>
<BR>
There is a sudden explosion of electrical energy and a wild howling aura of red light, and then silence.  After a few moment's pause, we hear someone climbing up the tree.  It is Malvasian, putting the potion high up in the bough.  He chuckles as he climbs back down and the curtain drops.<BR>
<BR>
Epilogue.<BR>
<BR>
The curtain rises on a road to Silvenar.  A gang of bandits have surrounded Malvasian, who is propped up on his staff, barely able to stand.  They pull his chest away from him with ease.<BR>
<BR>
BANDIT #1: What have we got here?  Don't you know it ain't safe to be out on the road, all sick like you are?  Why don't we help you with your load?<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN (weakly): Please ...  Let me be ...<BR>
<BR>
BANDIT #2: Go on, spellcaster, fight us for it!<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  I can't ... too weak ...<BR>
<BR>
Suddenly, Inzoliah flies in, casting lightning bolts from her fingers at the bandits, who quickly scramble away.  She lands on the ground and picks up the chest.  Malvasian collapses, dying.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN:  Hypothetically, what if ... a battlemage cast a spell on another which didn't harm him at once, but ... drained his life force and his magicka, bit by bit, so he wouldn't know at the time, but ... feel confident enough to leave the potion of healing behind?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: A most treacherous battlemage she'd be.<BR>
<BR>
MALVASIAN: And ... hypothetically ... would she be likely to help her fallen foe ... so that she could enjoy the humiliation of him continuing ... to live?<BR>
<BR>
INZOLIAH: From my experience, hypothetically, no.  She doesn't sound like a fool.<BR>
<BR>
As Inzoliah lugs the chest off toward Silvenar, and Malvasian expires on the stage, we drop the curtain.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
莫须有的背叛<BR>
独幕剧<BR>
安希尔·默维尔　著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
剧中人物<BR>
马瓦西安：高精灵战斗法师<BR>
英佐莉亚：暗精灵战斗法师<BR>
多瑟图斯：西罗帝尔治疗师<BR>
希亚瓦斯：一个阿尔贡野蛮人<BR>
一个幽灵<BR>
几个强盗<BR>
<BR>
场景：艾尔登森林(Eldenwood)<BR>
<BR>
当帷幕升起，我们看到传说中瓦伦省，上古林地那雾蒙蒙的景色。四面八方都能听到狼嚎声。希亚瓦斯，一个满身是血鬼鬼祟祟的动物从树丛中跳出，环视着四周。<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：视野清晰。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚，一位秀丽的暗精灵法师在野蛮人帮助下从树上爬下。周围传来了迫近的脚步声。希亚瓦斯拔剑出鞘，英佐莉亚准备施法。什么也没有出现。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：你伤的很重。你该让多瑟图斯给你疗伤。<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：他的法力已经在洞里耗光了。我很好。如果我们能从这里出去，并且没人用得着最后这瓶药剂的话，它就归我了。马瓦西安在哪？<BR>
<BR>
高精灵战斗法师马瓦西安和西罗帝尔治疗师多瑟图斯在树丛中现身，两人抬着一个很重的箱子。他们笨茁地搬着战利品走出树丛。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：我来了，但我不明白为什么我要扛这么重的东西。我一直认为和一个伟大的野蛮人一起钻研地牢的好处就是他能带着所有的战利品。<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：如果搬着东西，我就无法腾出双手战斗。如果觉得我说错了就反驳我，但你们三个谁也没有足够的法力从这里出去。在电死和烧死地下那个矮人后你们就没法力了。<BR>
<BR>
多瑟图斯：是很多矮人。<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：别担心，我不会干那种事。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚（径直地）：你什么意思？<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：杀了你们，然后独吞那件黑檀甲。承认吧——你一定觉得我有那种想法。<BR>
<BR>
多瑟图斯：多么完美而又可怕的想法。我从不觉得别人，不论是多么卑鄙与堕落的……<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：为什么不呢？<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：正如他自己说的那样，他需要搬运工。他不可能搬着箱子击退艾尔登森林的土著民。<BR>
<BR>
多瑟图斯：斯丹达尔说过，阿尔贡是典型的吝啬、狡诈……<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：那你为什么要让我活着？<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：我没必要让你活着，要不是你比其他两个长得更漂亮，外加我想得到一张光滑的毛皮。此外，如果有什么东西跟踪我们，你首先会成为它的猎物。<BR>
<BR>
附近的丛林里传来一阵嘈杂声。<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：去看看。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：可能是一只狼，树丛里到处都是。你去看一下。<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯：你有一个选择的机会，英佐莉亚。去那里，那你可能活下来；留在这，那你死定了。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚想了想，然后向树丛中走去。<BR>
<BR>
希亚瓦斯（对马瓦西安和多瑟图斯）：希尔维纳的王会为这副甲付个好价钱的，我们三人分脏会比四人分好得多。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：你说得很对啊。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚突然漂到舞台顶端。一个半透明的幽灵出现在丛林中，扑向另一个人，恰好是希亚瓦斯。当野蛮人尖叫着用剑砍它时，幽灵向他散出阵阵气体，希亚瓦斯倒在了地上。幽灵接着转向多瑟图斯，正当它集中精力向可怜的多瑟图斯施放寒冰魔法时，马瓦西安射出了一个火球，幽灵化为蒸汽消失在雾蒙蒙的天空中。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚落回地面，马瓦西安正查看多瑟图斯和希亚瓦斯的尸体，他们两个脸色苍白，看样子都中了幽灵吸取力量的魔法。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：你到底还是留了些魔力。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：你也一样。他们死了吗？<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安从多瑟图斯的包里拿走了治疗药水。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：是啊。好在药剂没有因他的倒下而破碎。好吧，现在只剩我们两个来收集战利品了。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：我们没有彼此就离不开这个地方，不管你是否愿意。<BR>
<BR>
两位战斗法师拾起箱子，迈着沉重的步子在灌木丛中小心地前进，时不时停下听着脚步声和其他奇怪的声音。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：让我确认一下，我知道你剩了一些魔力，于是你用它使希亚瓦斯成为幽灵的猎物，迫使我使用大多剩余的魔力消灭那个生物，这样我剩下的魔法就不及你了。真是一流的反应速度。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：谢谢。只是符合逻辑罢了。你还有力量再施放其他的魔法吗？<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：那是自然，一位有经验的战斗法师总是会一些小而高效的魔法来应对这样的战斗。我想你也在衣袖里藏了些小把戏吧？<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：当然，正如你说的那样。<BR>
<BR>
他们停了一会，当远处撕破天空的哀嚎渐渐消失，他们又步履艰难地上路了。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：就当是个智力测试，我想知道如果我们不再遇到任何战斗，当离开这里时你会用什么魔法对付我呢？<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：我希望你不是在暗示你想杀了我独吞财宝。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：当然不是，我也不会那样对你。只是做个智力测试。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：好，如果单纯是一个智力测试的话，我对你施一个蛭吸生命的魔法，这样可以夺走你的生命来治疗我自己。毕竟，在这到希尔维纳的路上有不少强盗，一个重伤的法师拿着贵重物品会成为及其诱人的猎物。我可不希望活着逃出了上古林地，却死在野外。<BR>

英佐莉亚：这是一个很合理的应答。只有我自己，再说一遍，我不是说自己想这么做，但我想一个小而突然的闪电魔法可以很好的达到我的目的。我知道强盗的危险，但别忘了我们还有一瓶治疗药剂呢。我可以轻松地杀了你，然后使自己痊愈。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
英佐莉亚：从逻辑上讲，是先喝到药剂的人——在这种情况下应该是你，因为你拿到它了。那么如果我们两个人都受伤了，但没有被杀死了呢？<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：逻辑上讲一个诡计多端的战斗法师会拿走药剂，留下他那受伤的同伴任由天命。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：那的确听起来是最明智的。但请想想战斗法师们尽管狡诈，却是尊重彼此的。比如，或许在那种情况下，胜利者会见药剂放在他或她的重伤的同伴身旁的树上。当受伤的那个恢复了魔力，他或她就可以浮空到树枝上拿到药剂。那个时候，胜利的一方早已拿走了战利品。<BR>
<BR>
两人听到丛林中的声音时停顿了一会。他们小心地爬过树枝以避开它。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：我明白你说的意思，但如果他或她让自己的受害者活下来，就有悖于我们假定的这个战斗法师的本性。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：或许你说的对，但我的观点是最狡诈的战斗法师会以打败了某人而沾沾自喜，并且会让那个人终生生活在耻辱之中。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：这些假定狡诈的战斗法师听起来……（激动地）天亮了！你听见了吗？<BR>
<BR>
他们两个快速爬过树枝并跳入后面的丛林中，已不在我们的视线内了。但我们可以看见太阳的微微光晕。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安（在高树丛后面）：我们成功了。<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚（也在高树丛后面）：的确如此。<BR>
<BR>
先是一阵闪电魔法的爆炸声和耀眼的红色光环，然后是一阵沉寂。过了一段时间，一个人爬树的声音。是马瓦西安，他把药剂高高地放在枝头，呵呵地笑着从树上爬回地面。帷幕降落下来。<BR>
<BR>
尾声。<BR>
<BR>
帷幕在希尔维纳的道路上再一次拉开。一帮强盗围着用木杖勉强支撑身体的马瓦西安，他们轻轻地抢走了他手中的宝箱。<BR>
<BR>
强盗#1：我们拿到了什么？难道你不知道，像你这样虚弱的人走在路上不安全吗？我们为什么不帮你减减负呢？<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安（虚弱地）：求求你……让我走……<BR>
<BR>
强盗#2：来呀，法师，和我们抢啊！<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：我不行了……没力气……<BR>
<BR>
突然，英佐莉亚飞来，从指尖向强盗们放出闪电魔法，他们很快爬着逃跑了。她落在地上并拾起箱子。马瓦西安倒在地上即将死亡。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：假如……一个战斗法师对另一个施放的魔法不会瞬间伤害他，但是……一点点地吸取他的耐力和魔力，他当时不知道，但……却自信地把药剂留下了会怎样？<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：她真是个狡猾的战斗法师。<BR>
<BR>
马瓦西安：那……如果……她愿意帮助倒下的敌人……以便品尝他苟且偷生的耻辱吗？<BR>
<BR>
英佐莉亚：据我的经验看，不会的，她听起来不是个傻瓜。<BR>
<BR>
当英佐莉亚拖着箱子朝希尔维纳走去时，马瓦西安在舞台上断了气，我们落下了帷幕。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Art of War Magic<BR>
by Zurin Arctus<BR>
with Commentary By Other Learned Masters<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Chapter 3:  Dispositions<BR>
<BR>
Master Arctus said:<BR>
<BR>
1. The moment to prepare your offense is the moment the enemy becomes vulnerable to attack.<BR>
<BR>
Leros Chael:  Knowledge of the enemy mage's mind is of the foremost importance.  Once you know his mind, you will know his weaknesses.<BR>
<BR>
Sedd Mar:  Master Arctus advised Tiber Septim before the battle of Five Bridges not to commit his reserves until the enemy was victorious.  Tiber Septim said, $93If the enemy is already victorious, what use committing the reserve?$94  To which Master Arctus replied, $93Only in victory will the enemy be vulnerable to defeat.$94  Tiber Septim went on to rout an enemy army twice the size of his.<BR>
<BR>
2. The enemy's vulnerability may be his strongest point; your weakness may enable you to strike the decisive blow.<BR>
<BR>
Marandro Ur:  In the wars between the Nords and the Chimer, the Nord shamans invariably used their mastery of the winds to call down storms before battle to confuse and dismay the Chimer warriors.  One day, a clever Chimer sorcerer conjured up an ice demon and commanded him to hide in the rocks near the rear of the Chimer army.  When the Nords called down the storms as usual, the Chimer warriors began to waver.  But the ice demon rose up as the storm struck, and the Chimer turned in fear from what they believed was a Nord demon and charged into the enemy line, less afraid of the storm than of the demon.  The Nords, expecting the Chimer to flee as usual, were caught off guard when the Chimer attacked out of the midst of the storm.  The Chimer were victorious that day.<BR>
<BR>
3. When planning a campaign, take account of both the arcane and the mundane.  The skillful battlemage ensures that they are in balance; a weight lifted by one hand is heavier than two weights lifted by both hands.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
4. When the arcane and mundane are in balance, the army will move effortlessly, like a swinging door on well-oiled hinges.  When they are out of balance, the army will be like a three-legged dog, with one leg always dragging in the dust.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
5. Thus when the army strikes a blow, it will be like a thunderclap out of a cloudless sky.  The best victories are those unforeseen by the enemy, but obvious to everyone afterwards.<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
6. The skillful battlemage ensures that the enemy is already defeated before the battle begins.  A close-fought battle is to be avoided; the fortunes of war may turn aside the most powerful sorcery, and courage may undo the best-laid plans.  Instead, win your victory ahead of time.  When the enemy knows he is defeated before the battle begins, you may not need to fight.<BR>
<BR>
7. Victory in battle is only the least kind of victory.  Victory without battle is the acme of skill.<BR>
<BR>
8. Conserving your power is another key to victory.  Putting forth your strength to win a battle is no demonstration of skill.  This is what we call tactics, the least form of the art of war magic.<BR>
<BR>
Thulidden dir'Tharkun:  By 'tactics', Master Arctus includes all the common battle magics.  These are only the first steps in an understanding of war magic.  Any hedge mage can burn up his enemies with fire.  Destroying the enemy is the last resort of the skillful battlemage.<BR>
<BR>
9. The battle is only a leaf on the tree; if a leaf falls, does the tree die?  But when a branch is lopped off, the tree is weakened; when the trunk is girdled, the tree is doomed.<BR>
<BR>
10. If you plan your dispositions well, your victories will seem easy and you will win no acclaim.  If you plan your dispositions poorly, your victories will seem difficult, and your fame will be widespread.<BR>
<BR>
Marandro Sul:  Those commonly believed to be the greatest practitioners of war magic are almost always those with the least skill.  The true masters are not known to the multitude.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
战法要术<BR>
祖林·阿克图斯　著<BR>
附其他大师的批注<BR><BR>

第三章：部署<BR>

<BR>
1.进攻之机只在敌军暴露弱点之时。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
赛德·玛尔：五桥战役前，阿克图斯大师曾忠告泰伯·塞普汀，敌人获胜之后再投入预备队。泰伯·塞普汀说，“既然敌人已经取胜，对他们攻击还有何用？”对此，阿克图斯大师回答说，“强大的敌人只有在胜利的时候才会变得脆弱可击”。泰伯·塞普汀遂彻底击败了数量为己方两倍的敌军。<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
马兰卓·乌尔：在诺德人和歧莫的战争中，诺德萨满总是一成不变地在战前利用他们对风的掌控召唤风暴去扰乱歧莫战士、打击他们的士气。有一天，一个聪明的歧莫术士召唤出一只冰魔并命令它藏在歧莫军队后面附近的岩石堆里。当诺德人像往常一样召唤风暴的时候，歧莫战士的军心开始动摇。但冰魔突然像风墙一样站了起来，歧莫以为这也是诺德人的魔鬼，恐惧让他们像潮水一样冲破敌人的阵线，毕竟魔鬼比风暴更为恐怖。那些诺德人，本来以为歧莫会像往常一样逃跑，结果在冲破风暴迷雾的歧莫战士的武力下束手就擒。那天，歧莫获得了胜利。<BR>
<BR>
3.在战争的筹划阶段，要通盘考虑到复杂和简单的情况。造诣深的战斗法师确信，它们两者必须兼顾；单手举重比双手举起两倍的重量更难。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
4.当复杂和简单的情况都通盘考虑到了，军队就能轻轻松松地前行了，就像是门轴加了油后可以随意转动一样。当两者没有考虑周全时，军队就像是三条腿的狗，一条腿总在扬起尘土。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
5.因此，当军队作战有力时，它就像万钧雷霆一般。最出色的胜利是那种敌军不可预见而事后对每个人来说又是显而易见的胜利。<BR>
<BR>
<BR>
6.造诣深的战斗法师总是能够胜于未战之时。一定要避免近身肉博；战争的时运可以扭转法力最强的魔咒，勇气可以让最好的计划搁置。相反的，要在战争开始前获得你的胜利。当敌人认识到自己未战先败，你就没必要再打了。<BR>
<BR>
7.战斗中的胜利只是低层次的胜利。不战而屈人之兵才是战争的最高艺术。<BR>
<BR>
8.保存实力是取得胜利的另一关键。为了取胜而过早地展现自己全部实力非高明之举。此之所谓战术，乃战法技艺之常识。<BR>
<BR>
苏里登·迪尔'塔康：通过战术，阿克图斯大师归纳所有常见的战斗魔法。这是理解战斗魔法的起点。任何防御法师都会用火烧死他们的敌人。毁灭敌人是造诣深的战斗法师采取的最后措施。<BR>
<BR>
9.一场战斗只是敌人实力之树的一块叶子；叶子掉了，树就死了吗？但是如果树枝被砍，树就会变弱；当树干被缠住，树也就被毁掉了。<BR>
<BR>
10.如果事先做好谋划，胜利就垂手可得，且不为大众所知。如果没有做好谋划，你就会赢得很艰难，亦将声名远播。<BR>
<BR>

The Mystery of Princess Talara, Part III<BR>
By Mera Llykith<BR><BR>

<BR>

<BR>
$93Protecting the Imperial interests in Camlorn is busy work, milord.  But I cannot imagine you would be interested in the minutiae of the ambassador's appointments.$94<BR>
<BR>

<BR>
$93She is a most comely wench,$94 laughed Lord Eryl. $93Have you noticed how much she resembles the late Princess Talara?$94<BR>
<BR>
$93I have only been in Camlorn for fifteen years, milord.  I never saw her late majesty.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93Now I could understand it if he had taken to writing poetry, but what man in love spends his days in the kitchens of the palace, talking to old servants?  That hardly sounds like molten passion to me, even based on my limited experience.$94 Lord Eryl rolled his eyes. $93And what is this business he has now in - oh, what is the name of that village?$94<BR>

I believe it's just to put a stamp on some deed that needs the Imperial seal.$94<BR>

<BR>
Seated in a tavern that smelled of mildew and sour beer, Lord Strale marveled at how the Emperor's agent Lady Brisienna always found the most public of places for her most private of conferences.  It was harvest time in Umbington, and all of the field hands were drinking away their meager wages in the noisiest of fashions.  He was dressed appropriately for the venue, rough trousers and a simple peasant's vest, but he still felt conspicuous.  In comparison to his two female companions, he certainly was.  The woman to his right was used to frequenting the low places of Daggerfall as a common prostitute.  Lady Brisienna to his left was even more clearly in her element.<BR>
<BR>
$93By what name would you prefer I call you?$94 Lady Brisienna asked solicitously.<BR>

$93I am used to the name Gyna, though that may have to change,$94 was her reply. $93Of course, it may not.  Gyna the Whore may be the name writ on my grave.$94<BR>

The only permanent solution is to capture those who would do you harm and then to raise you to your proper station.$94<BR>

<BR>

If your friend the ambassador hadn't investigated and discovered what he has, I would have dismissed you outright as a madwoman,$94 Brisienna laughed, forcing a smile onto Gyna's face to match. $93But now, yes, I do believe you.  Perhaps that makes me the madwoman.$94<BR>
<BR>

<BR>

What we have in your case is a very messy assassination that happened twenty years ago, and its aftermath.  If His Imperial Majesty involved itself in every bloody hiccup in the succession in each of his thousand vassal kingdoms, he would never accomplish anything for the greater good of Tamriel.$94<BR>
<BR>

In fact, I was leaving Camlorn and going back home to Daggerfall when I saw Lord Strale again.  He was the one who began this quest to resolve this, not me.  And when he brought me back, I only wanted to see my cousin to tell her who I was, but he forbade me.$94<BR>

But for this to turn out well, you must accomplish two things to the Emperor's satisfaction.  First, you must prove with absolute certainty who is the power behind this plot you've uncovered. When it was agreed what had to be done, Lady Brisienna took her leave to find her ally Proseccus.  Strale and Gyna set off to the west, toward Camlorn.  It was not long after beginning their ride through the woods that they heard the sound of galloping hoof beats far up ahead. Lord Strale quickly yanked Gyna from her horse, pulling her behind him.  He made a brief, deft motion with his hands.  A ring of flame materialized around them, and rushed outward, striking their assailants.  The men roared in pain and dropped to their knees.  Lord Strale jumped the horse over the closest one, and galloped at full speed westward.  <BR>

<BR>
$93I'm sorry, milord,$94 groaned Gnorbooth. $93I tried to warn you as soon as I could.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93In your next life, perhaps you'll remember not to trust your plans to a drunkard!$94 laughed Lord Eryl.  He had them in his sight, and the spell was unleashed.<BR>

Gnorbooth saw him first, by the light of the ball of fire that leapt from his fingertips.  Later, Lord Eryl was to wonder to himself what the fool had intended to do.  Perhaps he was rushing forward to pull Lord Strale out of the path.  Perhaps he was trying to flee the path of destruction, and had simply moved left when he should have moved right.  Perhaps, as unlikely as it seemed, he was willing to sacrifice himself to save his master.  Whatever the reason, the result was the same. <BR>
<BR>
He got in the way.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Breathing Water<BR>
by Haliel Myrm<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
He walked through the dry, crowded streets of Bal Fell, glad to be among so many strangers.  In the wharfs of Vivec, he had no such anonymity.  They knew him to be a smuggler, but here, he could be anyone.  A lower-class peddler perhaps.  A student even.  Some people even pushed against him as he walked past as if to say, $93We would not dream of being so rude as to acknowledge that you don't belong here.$94<BR>
<BR>
Seryne Relas was not in any of the taverns, but he knew she was somewhere, perhaps behind a tenement window or poking around in a dunghill for an exotic ingredient for some spell or another.  He knew little of the ways of sorceresses, but that they always seemed to be doing something eccentric.  Because of this prejudice, he nearly passed by the old Dunmer woman having a drink from a well.  It was too prosaic, but he knew from the look of her that she was Seryne Relas, the great sorceress.<BR>
<BR>
$93I have gold for you,$94 he said to her back. $93If you will teach me the secret of breathing water.$94<BR>
<BR>
She turned around, a wide wet grin stretched across her weathered features. $93I ain't breathing it, boy.  I'm just having a drink.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93Don't mock me,$94 he said, stiffly. $93Either you're Seryne Relas and you will teach me the spell of breathing water, or you aren't.  Those are the only possibilities.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93If you're going to learn to breath water, you're going to have to learn there are more possibilities than that, boy.   The School of Alteration is all about possibilities, changing patterns, making things be what they could be.  Maybe I ain't Seryne Relas, but I can teach how to breathe water,$94 she wiped her mouth dry. $93Or maybe I am Seryne Relas and I won't.  Or maybe even I can teach you to breath water, but you can't learn.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93I'll learn,$94 he said, simply.<BR>
<BR>
$93Why don't you just buy yourself a spell of water breathing or a potion over at the Mages Guild?$94 she asked.  $93That's how it's generally done.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93They're not powerful enough,$94 he said. $93I need to be underwater for a long time.  I'm willing to pay whatever you ask, but I don't want any questions.  I was told you could teach me.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93What's your name, boy?$94<BR>
<BR>
$93That's a question,$94 he replied.  His name was Tharien Winloth, but in Vivec, they called him the Tollman.  His job, such as it was, was collecting a percentage of the loot from the smugglers when they came into harbor to bring to his boss in the Camonna Tong.  Of the value of that percentage, he earned another percentage.  In the end it was very small indeed.  He had scarcely any gold of his own, and what he had, he gave to Seryne Relas.<BR>
<BR>
The lessons began that very day.  The sorceress brought her pupil, who she simply called $93boy,$94 out to a low sandbank along the sea.<BR>
<BR>
$93I will teach you a powerful spell for breathing water,$94 she said. $93But you must become a master of it.  As with all spells and all skills, you more you practice, the better you get.  Even that ain't enough.  To achieve true mastery, you must understand what it is you're doing.  It ain't simply enough to perform a perfect thrust of a blade -- you must also know what you are doing and why.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93That's common sense,$94 said Tharien<BR>
<BR>
$93Yes, it is,$94 said Seryne, closing her eyes. $93But the spells of Alteration are all about uncommon sense.  The infinite possibilities, breaking the sky, swallowing space, dancing with time, setting ice on fire, believing that the unreal may become real.  You must learn the rules of the cosmos and then break them.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93That sounds ... very difficult,$94 replied Tharien, trying to keep a straight face.<BR>
<BR>
Seryne pointed to the small silver fish darting along the water's edge: $93They don't find it so.  They breath water just fine.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93But that's not magic.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93What I'm saying to you, boy, is that it is.$94<BR>
<BR>
For several weeks, Seryne drilled her student, and the more he understood about what he was doing and the more he practiced, the longer he could breath underwater.  When he found that he could cast the spell for as long as he needed, he thanked the sorceress and bade her farewell.<BR>
<BR>
$93There is one last lesson I have to teach you,$94 she said. $93You must learn that desire is not enough.  The world will end your spell no matter how good you are, and no matter how much you want it.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93That's a lesson I'm happy not to learn,$94 he said, and left at once for the short journey back to Vivec.<BR>
<BR>
The wharfs were much the same, with all the same smells, the same sounds, and the same characters.  His boss had found a new Tollman, he learned from his mates. They were still looking out for the smuggler ship Morodrung, but they had given up hope of ever seeing it.   Tharien knew they would not.  He had seen it sink from the wharf a long time ago.<BR>
<BR>
On a moonless night, he cast his spell and dove into the thrashing purple waves.  He kept his mind on the world of possibilities, that books could sing, that green was blue, that that water was air, that every stroke and kick brought him closer to a sunken ship filled with treasure.  He felt magicka surge all around him as he pushed his way deeper down.  Ahead he saw a ghostly shadow of the Morodrung, its mast billowing in a wind of deep water currents.  He also felt his spell begin to fade.  He could break reality long enough to breath water all the way back up to the surface, but not enough to reach the ship.<BR>
<BR>
The next night, he dove again, and this time, the spell was stronger.  He could see the vessel in detail, clouded over and dusted in sediment.  The wound in its hull where it had struck the reef.  A glint of gold beckoning from within.  But still he felt reality closing in, and he had to surface.<BR>
<BR>
The third night, he made it into the steerage, past the bloated corpses of the sailors, nibbled and picked apart by fish.  Their glassy eyes bulging, their mouths stretched open.  Had they only known the spell, he thought briefly, but his mind was more occupied by the gold scattered along the floor, the boxes that contained them shattered.  He considered scooping as much he could carry into his pockets, but a sturdy iron box seemed to bespeak more treasures.<BR>
<BR>
On the wall was a row of keys.  He took each down and tried it on the locked box, but none opened it.  One key, however, was missing.  Thalien looked around the room.  Where could it be?  His eyes went to the corpse of one of the sailors, floating in a dance of death not far from the box, his hands tightly clutching something.  It was a key.  When the ship had begun to sink, this sailor had evidently gone for the iron box.  Whatever was in it had to be very valuable.<BR>
<BR>
Thalien took the sailor's key and opened the box.  It was filled with broken glass.  He rummaged around until he felt something solid, and pulled out two flasks of some kind of wine.  He smiled as he considered the foolishness of the poor alcoholic.  This was what was important to the sailor, out of all the treasure in the Morodrung. <BR>
<BR>
Then, suddenly, Thalien Winloth felt reality.<BR>
<BR>
He had not been paying attention to the grim, tireless advance of the world on his spell.  It was fading away, his ability to breath water.  There was no time to surface.  There was no time to do anything.  As he sucked in, his lungs filled with cold, briny water.<BR>
<BR>
A few days later, the smugglers working on the wharf came upon the drowned body of the former Tollman.  Finding a body in the water in Vivec was not in itself noteworthy, but the subject that they discussed over many bottles of flin was how did it happen that he drowned with two potions of water breathing in his hands.<BR>

“我有金子要给你，”他对她说。“如果你能教我水下呼吸的秘诀。”<BR>
<BR>
她转过身来，一个湿漉漉的笑容在她那饱经风霜的脸庞上延展开来。“我可没呼吸，孩子。我只是喝了一口。”<BR>
<BR>
“别嘲弄我，”他生硬地说。“要么你是赛琳·瑞拉斯，你要教会我水下呼吸的咒语，要么你不是。这是唯一的可能性。”<BR>
<BR>
“如果你要学会水下呼吸，你就必须知道还有更多的可能性，男孩。变化系学院遍地关于可能性，改变模式，让事情成为他们可能的模样。或许我不是赛琳·瑞拉斯，但我可以教如何水下呼吸，”她擦干嘴。“又或者我是赛琳·瑞拉斯，我不会。或者，我甚至可以教你水中呼吸，但你学不会。”<BR>
<BR>
“我能学会，”他简单回应。<BR>
<BR>
“你为什么不在法师公会给自己买条水下呼吸咒语或一瓶药水呢？”她问。“寻常情况都是这样的。”<BR>
<BR>
“它们不够强，”他说。“我需要在水下呆很长时间。我愿意支付你的任何要求，但我可不想有什么问题。我听说你可以教我。”<BR>
<BR>
“你叫什么名字，孩子？”<BR>
<BR>
“这是个问题，”他回答。他的名字叫塔里恩·温洛斯，但在维威克城，人们称他为“收费员”。他的工作就是从走私者那里收集一定比例的战利品，然后将他们带到港口带到卡莫纳堂的老板那里。在这个百分比的价值中，他赚了另一个百分比。最后它确实非常小。他自己的金子几乎没了，他所有的，都给了赛琳·瑞拉斯。<BR>
<BR>
课程从那天开始。女术士带着她的学生，她简称为“男孩”，来到海边的一个低矮的沙洲。<BR>
<BR>
“我会教你一个强大的水下呼吸咒语，”她说。“但你必须成为它的主人。与所有咒语和技能一样，你练习得越多，获得的效果就越好。即使这样还不够。为了达到真正的掌握，你必须明白你在做什么。仅仅完成一次完美的利刃猛击是不够的——你还必须知晓你在做些什么以及为什么。”<BR>
<BR>
“这是常识，”塔里恩说。<BR>
<BR>
“没错，是这样，”赛琳说，闭上了眼睛。“但变化系法术都是有关于不同寻常的感觉。无限可能，击破苍穹，吞噬空间，畅舞时间，燃火于冰，相信虚幻可能成为现实。你必须学遍宇宙规则，然后打破它们。”<BR>
<BR>
“这听起来……非常困难，”塔里恩回答，努力保持板着脸。<BR>
<BR>
赛琳指了指沿水边游来游去的银色小鱼：“它们可不这么认为。它们水下呼吸得很好。”<BR>
<BR>
“但这可不是魔法。”<BR>
<BR>
“我要对你说的是，男孩，世事如此。”<BR>
<BR>
几个星期以来，赛琳一直在训练她的学生，他越了解自己在做什么，练习得越多，他在水下呼吸的时间就越长。当他发现自己可以随心所欲地施法时，他感谢女术士并告别了她。<BR>
<BR>
“我要教你最后一课，”她说。“你必须明白，光有欲望是不够的。无论你多么优秀，无论你多么想要，世界都会终结你的咒语。”<BR>
<BR>
“这是我很高兴不去学习的一课，”他说，然后立即离开，踏上返回维威克城的短途旅行。<BR>
<BR>
码头大同小异，气味相同，声音相同，特质相同。他的老板找到了一个新的收费员，他从他的伙伴那里得知。他们还在寻找走私者的船“摩洛钻”，但他们已经放弃了寻到它的希望。塔里恩知道他们不可能寻到。他很久以前就看到它从码头沉没了。<BR>
<BR>
在一个无月之夜，他施了咒语，一头扎进了翻腾的紫色海浪中。他一直在想着一个充满可能性的世界，书本可以歌唱，绿色变成蓝色，海水就是空气，每一次敲击和踢腿都让他离一艘装满宝藏的沉船更近了一步。当他向更深处推进时，他感到魔法在他周围涌动。在前方，他看到了“摩洛钻”幽灵般的影子，它的桅杆在深水流的风中翻腾。他也感觉到自己的咒语开始消退。他可以打破现实足够长的时间来水中呼吸一直回到达水面，但不足以到达沉船。<BR>
<BR>
第二天晚上，他又跳下去了，这一次，咒语更强了。他可以详细地看到这艘船，上面布满了云层，尘土飞扬。触礁船体上的伤口，一股金色的光芒从里向你招手。但他仍然觉得现实正在逼近，他不得不浮出水面。<BR>
<BR>
第三天晚上，他登上了统舱，经过水手们臃肿的尸体，被鱼咬碎。他们玻璃般的眼睛凸出，嘴巴张开。如果他们只知道咒语，他想了想，但他的脑海里更多的是散落在地板上的黄金，装着它们的盒子都碎了。他想尽可能多地舀到口袋里，但一个坚固的铁盒似乎预示着更多的宝藏。<BR>
<BR>
墙上有一排钥匙。他把每一把都拿下来，在锁着的盒子上试了试，但没一把能打开它。然而，有一把钥匙不见了。塔里恩环视房间。它可能在哪里？他的目光投向了其中一名水手的尸体，尸体在离箱子不远的地方跳起了死亡之舞，双手紧紧地抓着什么东西。那是一把钥匙。当船开始下沉的时候，这个水手显然是去找铁箱了。里面的任何东西都显然非常有价值。<BR>
<BR>
塔里恩接过水手的钥匙，打开了盒子。里面装满了碎玻璃。他四处翻找，直到感觉到有什么坚实的东西，然后拿出两瓶某种酒水。当他想到可怜愚蠢的酒鬼时，他微笑了。这对水手来说是最重要的，在“摩洛钻”的所有宝藏中。<BR>
<BR>
然后，突然，塔里恩·温洛斯感觉到了现实。<BR>
<BR>
他并没有注意到他的咒语——这个世界残酷而不知疲倦地行进——水下呼吸能力，正在消失。没时间浮出水面。亦没时间做出任何举动。随着他的吸吮，他的肺里充满了冰冷的咸水。<BR>
<BR>
几天后，在码头工作的走私者发现了前收费员的溺亡尸体。在维威克城的水下找到一具尸体本身并不值得关注，但他们在许多瓶弗林中讨论的主题是，他是如何因手里拿着两瓶“水中呼吸”而溺亡的。<BR>
<BR>"""

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Dragon Break Reexamined<BR>
by Fal Droon<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
The late 3rd era was a period of remarkable religious ferment and creativity. The upheavals of the reign of Uriel VII were only the outward signs of the historical forces that would eventually lead to the fall of the Septim Dynasty. The so called "Dragon Break" was first proposed at this time, by a wide variety of cults and fringe sects across the Empire, connected only by a common obsession with the events surrounding Tiber Septim's rise to power -- the "founding myth", if you will, of the Septim Dynasty.<BR>
<BR>
The basis of the Dragon Break doctrine is now known to be a rather prosaic error in the timeline printed in the otherwise authoritative "Encyclopedia Tamrielica", first published in 3E 12, during the early years of Tiber Septim's reign. At that time, the archives of Alinor were still inaccessible to human scholars, and the extant records from the Alessian period were extremely fragmentary. The Alessians had systematically burned all the libraries they could find, and their own records were largely destroyed during the War of Righteousness.<BR>
<BR>
The author of the Encyclopedia Tamrielica was apparently unfamiliar with the Alessian "year", which their priesthood used to record all dates. We now know this refers to the length of the long vision-trances undertaken by the High Priestess, which might last anywhere from a few weeks to several months. Based on analysis of the surviving trance scrolls, as well as murals and friezes from Alessian temples, I estimate that the Alessian Order actually lasted only about 150 years, rather than the famous "one thousand and eight years" given by the Encyclopedia Tamrielica. The "mystery" of the millennial-plus rule of the Alessians was accepted but unexplained until the spread of the Lorkhan cults in the late 3rd era, when the doctrine of the Dragon Break took hold. Because this dating (and explanation) was so widely held at the time, and then repeated by historians down through today, it has come to have the force of tradition. Recall, however, that the 3rd era historians were already separated from the Alessians by a gulf of more than 2,000 years. And history was still in its infancy, relying on the few archives from those early days.<BR>
<BR>
Today, modern archaeology and paleonumerology have confirmed what my own research in Alessian dating first suggested: that the Dragon Break was invented in the late 3rd era, based on a scholarly error, fueled by obsession with eschatology and Numidiumism, and perpetuated by scholarly inertia.<BR>
<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
龙破·重新审视<BR>
法尔·德隆　著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
第三纪元后期是一个宗教活动和创造力显著的时期。尤利尔七世统治时期的动荡只是历史力量的外在迹象，这些力量最终会导致塞普汀王朝的灭亡。所谓的“龙破”最早是在这个时候由帝国各地的各种异端和边缘教派提出的，它们只与围绕泰伯·塞普汀掌权事件的共同痴迷联系在一起——若你愿意的话，称为塞普汀王朝的“建国神话”。<BR>
<BR>
现在已知，龙破学说的基础是泰伯·塞普汀统治初年出版的权威性的《泰姆瑞尔的百科全书》中印刷的时间线中的一个相当平淡无奇的错误。当时，艾林诺的档案仍然是人类学者无法访问的，而阿莱西亚时期的现存记录极其零碎。阿莱西亚后人有计划地烧毁了他们能找到的所有图书馆，他们自己的记录在“正义之战”期间基本上被摧毁。<BR>
<BR>
《泰姆瑞尔的百科全书》的作者显然不熟悉阿莱西亚“年”，他们的神职人员用它来记录所有日期。我们现在知道，这指的是大祭司进行的长时间的情景神隐，可能会持续几周到几个月不等。根据对幸存的神隐卷轴以及阿莱西亚神殿的壁画和雕板的分析，我估计阿莱西亚教团实际上只持续了大约150年，而不是百科全书所给出的著名的“一千零八年”。阿莱西亚后人千年以上统治的“奥秘”被接受但无法解释，直到第三纪元末期洛克汗教派的传播，当龙破教义盛行时。因为这种年代测定（和解释）在当时被广泛接受，然后被历史学家重复到今天，它已经具有传统的力量。然而，请回想一下，第三纪元的历史学家已经与阿莱西亚后人相隔了2000多年的鸿沟。历史还处于起步阶段，依赖于早期的少数档案。<BR>
<BR>
今天，现代考古学和古命理学证实了我自己在阿莱西亚断代中的研究首先表明的内容：“龙破”是在第三纪元晚期发明的，基于一个学术错误，由对末世论和努米迪文兹姆的痴迷推动，并因学术惰性而延续。<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
维威克的三十六课：布道十三<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
那正是瑞斯代尼亚的岁月，歧莫与锻莫生活在奥姆希维及其勇士统谏使的英明仁慈统治之下。当维洛斯诸神退居其位，去塑造宇宙及其他事务时，统谏使时而会感到困惑。维威克总会在那里以此言相劝，此乃统治之王三课中的第二课：<BR>

The Lunar Lorkhan<BR>

I will not go into the varying accounts of what happened at Adamantine Tower, nor will I relate the War of Manifest Metaphors that rendered those stories unable to support most qualities of what is commonly known as "narrative." 一个小时之后，波特玛正在返回的路上。走过那精心修剪过的灌木丛的时候，波特玛注意到前面有一个黑色的身影，而那影子也发觉到了王后的脚步声，把自己藏到了屋檐下面。波特玛也曾经被人盯梢过，但是这次，不同的是，这个人的位置离她的卧室实在是太近了。波特玛马上把母亲给的项链给带了起来。<BR>
<BR>
“出来，走到我能看得到你的位置”她命令道。<BR>
<BR>
那个人从暗影里走了出来。波特玛观察了一下，一个暗肤色的中年人，披着一身染成黑色的山羊皮。在法术的作用下，他的眼睛直直地看着前方。<BR>
<BR>
“你替谁办事？”<BR>

“安提奥楚斯王子，他是我的主人”他以了无生气的声音说，“我是他的密探”<BR>
<BR>
波特玛突然有了一个主意。“王子他现在书房吗？”<BR>

<BR>
正当窗户刚刚关上的时候，外面传来了敲门声。进来的是间谍总管，他朝王子笑了一笑，呈给他一份东西。<BR>
<BR>
“这是什么？”安提奥楚斯揉了揉他的眼睛，“我想我现在一定还没清醒，这玩意在我看来简直就是是兽人的涂鸦”<BR>

<BR>
安提奥楚斯本想起身穿戴整齐，同时打发同床的女人出去，但随后否定了这一想法，他觉得现在这样会更好。“把她带进来吧，我就想羞辱下这女人”<BR>

<BR>
安提奥楚斯突然笑了出来。他朝他的间谍总管眨了眨眼睛。“啊，我现在还记得我妹妹进入我放黄色书刊的地方，拿里面的东西敲诈我的样子。说来，那也快20年了吧。可我记得清楚得很。你也应该已经发现，跟当年的破铜烂锁相比，现在这里换上的可是高级货。我猜，要是你不自己亲自出马的话，恐怕结果会让你狠狠地失望的”<BR>
<BR>
波特玛对此淡然一笑。这又如何呢？她认为自己已经彻底占了上风。<BR>

波特玛继续保持着微笑，心想安提奥楚斯好像还没有她想象中的那么笨。<BR>

<BR>

<BR>

<BR>
波特玛愤怒地摇着头，说不出话来。<BR>
<BR>
“把你手上的那份破烂货给我，去外边的雨里好好冷静冷静。在这之后，我要你把你阻止我登上皇位的计划全部的一字不漏的说出来”安提奥楚斯盯着波特玛的眼睛，“记住，我才是皇帝，狼女王。好了，现在你可以走了。”<BR>
<BR>
波特玛交出了那封信，转身离开房间。在外面的走廊上，她沉默了好久，只是出神地看着银色的雨珠在大理石墙上顺着那细细的，几乎看不到的裂缝滑下。<BR>
<BR>
“是的，也许你会登基的，哥哥”她说，“但是你在皇位上待不了太长的”<BR>

The people have come to accept it.  They bury their dead by daylight, and are away before Masser and Secunda have risen and the evil comes forth.  The only victims to fall prey to the devils within are the very stupid and the outsiders.$94<BR>

They're offering a fortune, so I accepted the assignment with the caveat that I could assemble my own team to split the reward.  That's why I've sought you each out.  From what I've heard, you, Nitrah, are the best bladesman in Morrowind.$94<BR>

$93Quarra, the most savage of the vampire bloodlines,$94 said Phlaxith. $93We have to find and exterminate each and every one.$94<BR>

Delving into the crypts, the group hounded out more of the creatures.  Though they varied in appearance, each seemed to rely on their strength and claws for attacking, and subtlety did not seem to be the style of any.  When the entire mausoleum had been searched and every creature within destroyed, the four finally made their way to the surface.  It was only an hour until sunrise.<BR>
<BR>
There was no frenzied scream or howl.  Nothing rushed forward towards them.  The final attack when it happened was so unlike the others that the questors were taken utterly by surprise.<BR>
<BR>
The ancient creature waited until the four were almost out of the cemetery, talking amiably, making plans for spending their share of the reward.  He judged carefully who would be the greatest threat, and then launched himself at the sorceress.  Had Phlaxith not turned his attention back from the gate, she would have been ripped to shreds before she had a chance to scream.<BR>
<BR>
The vampire knocked Massitha across a stone, its claws raking across her back, but stopped its assault in order to block a blow from Phlaxith's sword.  It accomplished this maneuver in its own brutal way, by tearing the warrior's arm from its socket.  Osmic and Nitrah set on it, but they found themselves in a losing battle.  Only when Massitha had pulled herself back up from behind the pile of rocks, weak and bleeding, that the fight turned.  She cast a magickal ball of flame at the creature, which so enraged it that it turned back to her.  Nitrah saw her opening and took it, beheading the vampire with a stroke of her sword.<BR>
<BR>
$93So you do know some spells of destruction, like you said,$94 said Nitrah.<BR>
<BR>
$93And a few spells of healing too,$94 she said weakly. $93But I can't save Phlaxith.$94<BR>
<BR>
The warrior died in the bloodied dust before them.  The three were quiet as they traveled across the dawn-lit countryside back toward Necrom.  Massitha felt the throb of pain on her back intensify as they walked and then a gradual numbness like ice spread through her body.<BR>
<BR>
$93I need to go to a healer and see if I've been diseased,$94 she said as they reached the city.<BR>
<BR>
$93Meet us at the Moth and Fire tomorrow morning,$94 said Nitrah. $93We'll go to the Temple and get our reward and split it there.$94<BR>
<BR>
Three hours later, Osmic and Nitrah sat in their room at the tavern, happily counting and recounting the gold marks.  Split three ways, it was a very comfortable sum.<BR>
<BR>
$93What if the healers can't do anything for Massitha?$94 smiled Osmic dreamily. $93Some diseases can be insidious.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93Did you hear something in the hall?$94 asked Nitrah quickly, but when she looked, there was no one there.  She returned, shutting the door behind her. $93I'm sure Massitha will survive if she went straight to the healer.  But we could leave tonight with the gold.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93Let's have one last drink to our poor sorceress,$94 said Osmic, leading Nitrah out of the room toward the stairs down.<BR>
<BR>
Nitrah laughed. $93Those spells of illusion won't help her track us down, as useful as she keeps saying they are.  Paralysis, light, silence -- not so good when you don't know where to look.$94<BR>
<BR>
They closed the door behind them.<BR>
<BR>
$93Invisibility is another spell of illusion,$94 said Massitha's disembodied voice.  The gold on the table rose in the air and vanished from sight as she slipped it into her purse.  The door again opened and closed, and all was silent until Osmic and Nitrah returned a few minutes later.<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
Palla<BR>
Book I<BR>
by Vojne Mierstyyd<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Palla.  Pal La.  I remember when I first heard that name, not long ago at all.  It was at a Tales and Tallows ball at a very fine estate west of Mir Corrup, to which I and my fellow Mages Guild initiates had found ourselves unexpectedly invited.  Truth be told, we needn't have been too surprised.  There were very few other noble families in Mir Corrup -- the region had its halcyon days as a resort for the wealthy far back in the 2nd era -- and on reflection, it was only appropriate to have sorcerers and wizards present at a supernatural holiday.  Not that we were anything more exotic than students at a small, nonexclusive charterhouse of the Guild, but like I said, there was a paucity of other choices available.<BR>
<BR>
For close to a year, the only home I had known was the rather ramshackle if sprawling grounds of the Mir Corrup Mages Guild.  My only companions were my fellow initiates, most of which only tolerated me, and the masters, whose bitterness at being at a backwater Guild prompted never-ending abuse.<BR>
<BR>
Immediately the School of Illusion had attracted me.  The Magister who taught us recognized me as an apt pupil who loved not only the spells of the science but their philosophical underpinnings.  There was something about the idea of warping the imperceptible energies of light, sound, and mind that appealed to my nature.  Not for me the flashy schools of destruction and alteration, the holy schools of restoration and conjuration, the practical schools of alchemy and enchantment, or the chaotic school of mysticism.  No, I was never so pleased as to take an ordinary object and by a little magic make it seem something other than what it was.<BR>
<BR>
It would have taken more imagination than I had to apply that philosophy to my monotonous life.  After the morning's lessons, we were assigned tasks before our evening classes.  Mine had been to clean out the study of a recently deceased resident of the Guild, and categorize his clutter of spellbooks, charms, and incunabula.<BR>
<BR>
It was a lonely and tedious appointment.  Magister Tendixus was an inveterate collector of worthless junk, but I was reprimanded any time I threw something away of the least possible value.  Gradually I learned enough to deliver each of his belongings to the appropriate department: potions of healing to the Magisters of Restoration, books on physical phenomena to the Magisters of Alteration, herbs and minerals to the Alchemists, and soulgems and bound items to the Enchanters.  After one delivery to the Enchanters, I was leaving with my customary lack of appreciation, when Magister Ilther called me back.<BR>
<BR>
$93Boy,$94 said the portly old man, handing me back one item. $93Destroy this.$94<BR>
<BR>
It was a small black disc covered with runes with a ring of red-orange gems like bones circling its periphery.<BR>
<BR>
$93I'm sorry, Magister,$94 I stammered. $93I thought it was something you'd be interested in.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93Take it to the great flame and destroy it,$94 he barked, turning his back on me. $93You never brought it here.$94<BR>
<BR>
My interest was piqued, because I knew the only thing that would make him react in such a way.  Necromancy.  I went back to Magister Tendixus's chamber and poured through his notes, looking for any reference to the disc.  Unfortunately, most of the notes had been written in a strange code that I was powerless to decipher.  I was so fascinated by the mystery that I nearly arrived late for my evening class in Enchantment, taught by Magister Ilther himself.<BR>
<BR>
For the next several weeks, I divided my time categorizing the general debris and making my deliveries, and researching the disc.  I came to understand that my instinct was correct: the disc was a genuine necromantic artifact.  Though I couldn't understand most of the Magister's notes, I determined that he thought it to be a means of resurrecting a loved one from the grave.<BR>
<BR>
Sadly, the time came when the chamber had been categorized and cleared, and I was given another assignment, assisting in the stables of the Guild's menagerie.  At least finally I was working with some of my fellow initiates and had the opportunity of meeting the common folk and nobles who came to the Guild on various errands.  Thus was I employed when we were all invited to the Tales and Tallows ball.<BR>
<BR>
If the expected glamour of the evening were not enough, our hostess was reputed to be young, rich, unmarried orphan from Hammerfell.  Only a month or two before had she moved to our desolate, wooded corner of the Imperial Province to reclaim an old family manorhouse and grounds.  The initiates at the Guild gossiped like old women about the mysterious young lady's past, what had happened to her parents, why she had left or been driven from her homeland.  Her name was Betaniqi, and that was all we knew.<BR>
<BR>
 We wore our robes of initiation with pride as we arrived for the ball.  At the enormous marble foyer, a servant announced each of our names as if we were royalty, and we strutted into the midst of the revelers with great puffery.  Of course, we were then promptly ignored by one and all.  In essence, we were unimportant figures to lend some thickness to the ball.  Background characters.<BR>
<BR>
The important people pushed through us with perfect politeness.  There was old Lady Schaudirra discussing diplomatic appointments to Balmora with the Duke of Rimfarlin.  An orc warlord entertained a giggling princess with tales of rape and pillage.  Three of the Guild Magisters worried with three painfully thin noble spinsters about the haunting of Daggerfall.  Intrigues at the Imperial and various royal courts were analyzed, gently mocked, fretted over, toasted, dismissed, evaluated, mitigated, admonished, subverted.  No one looked our way even when we were right next to them.  It was as if my skill at illusion had somehow rendered us all invisible.<BR>
<BR>
I took my flagon out to the terrace.  The moons were doubled, equally luminous in the sky and in the enormous reflecting pool that stretched out into the garden.  The white marble statuary lining the sides of the pool caught the fiery glow and seemed to burn like torches in the night.  The sight was so otherworldly that I was mesmerized by it, and the strange Redguard figures immortalized in stone.  Our hostess had made her home there so recently that some of the sculptures were still wrapped in sheets that billowed and swayed in the gentle breeze.  I don't know how long I stared before I realized I wasn't alone.<BR>
<BR>
She was so small and so dark, not only in her skin but in her clothing, that I nearly took her for a shadow.  When she turned to me, I saw that she was very beautiful and young, not more than seventeen.<BR>
<BR>
$93Are you our hostess?$94 I finally asked.<BR>
<BR>
$93Yes,$94 she smiled, blushing. $93But I'm ashamed to admit that I'm very bad at it.  I should be inside with my new neighbors, but I think we have very little in common.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93It's been made abundantly clear that they hope I have nothing in common with them either,$94 I laughed.  $93When I'm a little higher than an initiate in the Mages Guild, they might see me as more of an equal.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93I don't understand the concept of equality in Cyrodiil yet,$94 she frowned. $93In my culture, you proved your worth, not just expected it.  My parents both were great warriors, as I hope to be.$94<BR>
<BR>
Her eyes went out to the lawn, to the statues.<BR>
<BR>
$93Do the sculptures represent your parents?$94<BR>
<BR>
$93That's my father Pariom there,$94 she said gesturing to a life-sized representation of a massively built man, unashamedly naked, gripping another warrior by the throat and preparing to decapitate him with an outstretched blade.  It was clearly a realistic depiction.  Pariom's face was plain, even slightly ugly with a low forehead, a mass of tangled hair, stubble on his cheeks.  Even a slight gap in his teeth, which no sculptor would surely have invented except to do justice to his model's true idiosyncrasies.<BR>
<BR>
$93And your mother?$94 I asked, pointing to a nearby statue of a proud, rather squat warrior woman in a mantilla and scarf, holding a child.<BR>
<BR>
$93Oh no,$94 she laughed. $93That was my uncle's old nurse.  Mother's statue still has a sheet over it.$94<BR>
<BR>
I don't know what prompted me to insist that we unveil the statue that she pointed to.  In all likelihood, it was nothing but fate, and a selfish desire to continue the conversation.   I was afraid that if I did not give her a project, she would feel the need to return to the party, and I would be alone again.  At first she was reluctant.  She had not yet made up her mind whether the statues would suffer in the wet, sometimes cold Cyrodilic climate.  Perhaps all should be covered, she reasoned.  It may be that she was merely making conversation, and was reluctant as I was to end the stand-off and be that much closer to having to return to the party.<BR>
<BR>
In a few minutes time, we tore the tarp from the statue of Betaniqi's mother.  That is when my life changed forevermore.<BR>
<BR>
She was an untamed spirit of nature, screaming in a struggle with a misshapen monstrous figure in black marble.  Her gorgeous, long fingers were raking across the creature's face.  The monster's talons gripped her right breast in a sort of caress that prefaces a mortal wound.  Its legs and hers wound around one another in a battle that was a dance.  I felt annihilated.  This lithe but formidable woman was beautiful beyond all superficial standards.  Whoever had sculpted it had somehow captured not only a face and figure of a goddess, but her power and will.  She was both tragic and triumphant.  I fell instantly and fatally in love with her.<BR>
<BR>
I had not even noticed when Gelyn, one of my fellow initiates who was leaving the party, came up behind us.  Apparently I had whispered the word $93magnificent,$94 because I heard Betaniqi reply as if miles away, $93Yes, it is magnificent.  That's why I was afraid of exposing it to the elements.$94<BR>
<BR>
Then I heard, clearly, like a stone breaking water, Gelyn: $93Mara preserve me.  That must be Palla.$94<BR>
<BR>
$93Then you heard of my mother?$94 asked Betaniqi, turning his way.<BR>
<BR>
$93I hail from Wayrest, practically on the border to Hammerfell.  I don't think there's anyone who hasn't heard of your mother and her great heroism, ridding the land of that abominable beast.  She died in that struggle, didn't she?$94<BR>
<BR>
$93Yes,$94 said the girl sadly. $93But so too did the creature.$94<BR>
<BR>
For a moment, we were all silent.  I don't remember anything more of that night.  Somehow I knew I was invited to dine the next evening, but my mind and heart had been entirely and forever more arrested by the statue.  I returned back to the Guild, but my dreams were fevered and brought me no rest.  Everything seemed diffused by white light, except for one beautiful, fearsome woman.  Palla.<BR>

帕拉<BR>
卷一<BR>
佛吉尼·密尔斯泰德　著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
帕拉。帕·拉。我记得我第一次听到这个名字的时候，就在不久之前。那是在米尔·科鲁普以西一处非常漂亮的庄园举行的烛圣节舞会，我和我的法师公会同修们意外地被邀请了。说实话，我们不必太惊讶。米尔·科鲁普几乎没有其他贵族家庭——该地区在遥远的第二纪元曾作为富人的度假胜地度过了宁静的日子——况且，在这种超自然的节日里，只有术士和法师出席才合适。不是因为作为又小又不起眼的法师公会分行学生的我们有多特别，而是像我说的，可有的选择实在是太少了。<BR>
<BR>
将近一年来，我仅有的家就是摇摇欲坠的米尔·科鲁普法师公会了。我唯一的伙伴就是我的新入会的同修。他们中的大部分仅仅是容忍我而已。而导师们，待在这个死气沉沉的公会里的苦闷，激发了无尽的虐骂。<BR>
<BR>
幻术学派立刻吸引了我。教导我们的先生认为我是个聪敏的学生，不但热爱魔法的咒语，还爱它们的哲学意义。把光电、声音和思想的微妙能量扭曲的理念吸引着我。不是闪耀的毁灭和变化学派，不是神圣的恢复和召唤学派，不是实用的炼金和附魔，也不是混乱的神秘学派。不，我从未这么愉悦过——对一个普通的物品施小小的魔法，使其看起来是另外一个物体。<BR>
<BR>
要将这个理念应用于我单调的生活上，所需的想象力要比我所有的多得多。晨课之后，晚课之前，我们被分派任务。我的是清理公会里一位最近去世的成员的书房，将他乱七八糟的咒语书、魔法项链和古书等等分门别类。<BR>
<BR>
这是一个孤单而无聊的任务。坦迪克萨斯导师是个根深蒂固的破烂收集者，但是每次我扔掉毫无价值的物品时都会被责备。逐渐地我学会了将他的每件所有物递送到相应的部门：恢复药水到恢复学派老师处，物理现象书籍到变化学派老师处，药草和矿物到炼金术士处，灵魂石和附魔物品到附魔师处。在一次给附魔师递送后，在我惯常的毫无感激地离开时，伊尔瑟老师把我叫了回来。<BR>
<BR>
“小子，”肥老头说着，把一件东西递给我。“毁了它。”<BR>
<BR>
那是一个覆盖咒文的黑色小碟，周围镶嵌着一圈像骨头似的红橙宝石。<BR>
<BR>
“对不起，先生，”我结结巴巴地说。“我以为这东西你会感兴趣。”<BR>
<BR>
“把它丢到火里烧掉，”他咆哮着，背对着我。“你从没把它带过来。”<BR>
<BR>
我的兴趣被激起了，因为我知道只有一样东西才能让他如此反应。死灵术。我回到坦迪克萨斯先生的房间，一心扑到他的笔记上，找关于碟子的任何记载。不幸的是，大部分笔记是用一种我无法解读的奇怪符号书写的。我对这个秘密太着迷了，以致伊尔瑟先生教授的附魔晚课差点迟到。<BR>
<BR>
接下来的几个星期里，我的时间都用作整理、递送，还有研究碟子上了。我认识到我的直觉是正确的：这个碟子是货真价实的死灵法术物品。虽然我不能理解老师的大部分笔记，我判定他想藉它将爱人从墓中复活。<BR>
<BR>
可悲的是，房间被整理干净的时候来临了。我也被分派了另外一个任务，在公会的马厩里做助手。终于我可以和其他新入会同伙们一起做工，有机会见到因各种差事来公会的平民和贵族了。所以我们都被邀请到烛圣节舞会。<BR>
<BR>
如果当晚的珠光宝气还嫌不够的话，我们的女主人是来自落锤的年轻富有的未婚孤儿。不到一两个月前她才搬到我们这个偏远的、树林繁茂的帝国边城，来回收古老家族庄园和领地。公会的新入会者们像老女人一样对这个神秘年轻女子的过去说三道四。她父母发生了什么事，她为什么离开或者被驱逐出她的故土。她的名字叫贝坦妮琪，而这就是我们知道的全部了。<BR>
<BR>
当我们到达参加舞会时，我们自豪地穿着我们的入会长袍。在巨大的大理石门厅里，一个仆人宣读了我们所有人的名字，恍若皇族，我们大摇大摆地走进狂欢者之中。当然，我们很快就被所有人忽略了。当然，我们立即就被忽视了。事实上，我们只是充舞会人数的无关角色。背景板。<BR>
<BR>
重要人士带着完美的优雅穿过我们。老肖迪拉女勋爵和瑞姆法林的公爵讨论到巴尔莫拉的外交任务。一个兽人军阀用强暴和掠夺的故事取悦一个嗤嗤笑着的公主。三位公会的老师和三个瘦骨如柴的贵族老处女为匕落的闹鬼担忧。帝都和几个皇室宫廷的阴谋斗争被分析、轻嘲、搅乱、祝酒、拒绝、评估、缓和、督促、推翻。即使我们就在他们身旁也没人看我们这边。就好像我的幻术技巧让我们都隐形了。<BR>
<BR>
我拿着酒杯来到了阳台。双月于空中与于花园里巨大的反射池里同等明亮。伫立在池边的雕像捕捉了炽热的光芒，仿如夜中火把般燃烧。这景致如此超脱尘俗，以致我被它催眠，奇异的红卫人雕像在石中不朽。我们的女主人最近才搬来，有些雕塑甚至尚裹在随微风翻滚摇摆的布里。我不知道我凝视了多久，直到意识到我并非一人。<BR>
<BR>
她是那么小那么黑，不仅仅是她的皮肤，还有她的衣服，让我差点以为她是一个影子。当她转向我的时候，我看到她是那么的漂亮年轻，不过十七岁。<BR>
<BR>
“你是我们的女主人吗？”我终于问到。<BR>
<BR>
“是的”她笑着，脸红了，“但是我很惭愧地承认我是个糟透的主人。我应该在里面和我的新邻居一起，但是我觉得我们的共通之处太少了。”<BR>
<BR>
“很显然他们也希望我和他们没有共通之处，”我大笑，“当我在法师公会里级别比新入会高一点时，他们或许会更加平等看待我。”<BR>
<BR>
“我还是不明白西罗帝尔的平等概念，”她皱起眉毛，“在我的文化里，你证明你的价值，而不只是期望你的价值。我的父母都是伟大的战士，像我希望成为的那样。”<BR>
<BR>
她的眼睛望向草坪，看着雕像。<BR>
<BR>
“这些雕像象征你的父母吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“在那里的是我的父亲帕瑞欧姆”她指着一个真人大小的魁伟男子雕像，他毫无羞耻的裸着体，紧扼着另一个战士的喉咙，准备用伸出来的利刃斩下他的头颅。这无疑是一个写实的表现。帕瑞欧姆的脸不好看，他前额低垂，一团纠结的乱发，双颊蓄着胡子，显得甚至有点丑陋。他牙齿还有个小缺口，除了想真实还原模特儿的特征之外，没有哪个雕塑家会这样创作。<BR>
<BR>
“是你母亲吗？”我问，手指着附近一个神态骄傲、身材矮胖的女战士雕像，她身披围巾头戴幔纱，抱着个孩子。<BR>
<BR>
“哦，不”她笑了，“那只是我叔叔的老保姆。我母亲的雕像还被布盖着呢。”<BR>
<BR>
我不知道是什么促使我坚持揭开她指着的雕像上的布。在所有可能性中，只能说是命运，和想继续谈话的自私欲望。我害怕如果我不给她一件事做，她会感到回到舞会去的需要，而我则会再次孤单一人。起先她不大情愿。她还没清楚雕像能否承受西罗帝尔潮湿又时而寒冷的气候。她推断也许全部雕像都应该盖上。可能她只是在有话找话，像我一样不愿结束与人疏远，要回到舞会上。<BR>
<BR>
几分钟内，我们揭开了贝坦妮琪母亲雕像的防水布。我的生活从此被改变。<BR>
<BR>
她是一个野性的精灵，尖叫着和一个黑色大理石雕成的畸形怪物搏斗。她漂亮而修长的手指抓着怪物的脸。怪物的魔爪带着些许抚爱地抓着她的右胸，引发了致命的伤口。它和她的腿在如舞蹈般的战斗中缠在一起。我被征服了。这个娇柔却又可畏的女子超越了一切肤浅的美的标准。不管是谁雕刻的，他不但捕捉到了这位女神的容貌和体形，还有她的力量和意志。她是悲剧的，也是胜利的。我即刻不幸地爱上了她。<BR>
<BR>
我甚至没有注意到盖尔林，正在离开舞会的我的同伴之一，来到了我们的身后。显然我低声说出了“美极了”这个词，因为我听到贝坦妮琪像在数里之外的回应，“是的，她美极了。这是我怕把她暴露在元素之中的原因。”<BR>
<BR>
然后我听到了，如石头击破水面般清晰，盖尔林说：“玛拉保佑我。那一定就是帕拉。”<BR>
<BR>
“那你一定听说过我母亲了？”贝坦妮琪问，转向他。<BR>
<BR>
“我来自途歇城，事实上就在落锤的边缘上。我不认为有谁没听说过你母亲和她伟大的英雄事迹，从那片土地上去除了这只可怕的怪兽。她在那场战斗中死去了，是吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“是的”女孩悲哀地说，“但是那只怪物也是。”<BR>
<BR>
一时间，我们都沉默了。我不记得那晚上还发生什么事了。但是我知道我被邀请第二天晚上来用餐，但是我的头脑和心灵都完全地、永远地被那雕像占据了。我回到公会，但我的梦想如火如荼，令我无眠。一切的一切都宛如被白光分散，仅有一位美丽而又令人敬畏的女子例外。帕拉。<BR>"""
