> BOOK.FNAM bk_RealBarenziah1
The Real Barenziah v I
《真实的巴兰兹娅·卷一》

> BOOK.TEXT bk_RealBarenziah1
"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
The Real Barenziah, Part 1<BR>
Anonymous<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
Five hundred years ago in Mournhold, City of Gems, there lived a blind widow and her only child, a tall, strapping young man.  He was a miner, as was his father before him, a common laborer in the mines of the Lord of Mournhold, for his ability in magicka was small.  The work was honorable but paid poorly.  His mother made and sold comberry cakes at the city market to help eke out their living.  They did well enough, she said, they had enough to fill their bellies, no one could wear more than one suit of clothing at a time, and the roof leaked only when it rained.  But Symmachus would have liked more.  He hoped for a lucky strike at the mines, which would garner him a large bonus.  In his free hours he enjoyed hoisting a mug of ale in the tavern with his friends, and gambling with them at cards.  He also drew the eyes and sighs of more than one pretty Elven lass, although none held his interest for long.  He was a typical young Dark Elf of peasant descent, remarkable only for his size.  It was rumored that he had a bit of Nordic blood in him.  <BR>
<BR>
In Symmachus' thirtieth year, there was great rejoicing in Mournhold-a girl-child had been born to the Lord and Lady.  A Queen, the people sang, a Queen is born to us!  For among the people of Mournhold, the birth of an heiress is a sure sign of future peace and prosperity.  <BR>
<BR>
When the time came round for the royal child's Rite of Naming, the mines were closed and Symmachus dashed home to bathe and dress in his best.  $93I'll rush straight home and tell you all about it,$94 he promised his mother, who would not be able to attend.  She had been ailing, and besides there would be a great crush of people as all Mournhold turned out to be part of the blessed event; and being blind she would be unable to see anything anyway.  <BR>
<BR>
$93My son,$94 she said.  $93Afore you go, fetch me a priest or a healer, else I may pass from the mortal plane ere you return.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus crossed to her pallet at once and noted anxiously that her forehead was very hot and her breathing shallow.  He pried loose a slat of the wooden floor under which their small hoard of savings was kept.  There wasn't nearly enough to pay a priest for healing.  He would have to give what they had and owe the rest.  Symmachus snatched up his cloak and hurried away.  <BR>
<BR>
The streets were full of folk hurrying to the sacred grove, but the temples were locked and barred.  $93Closed for the ceremony,$94 read all the signs.  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus elbowed his way through the mob and managed to overtake a brown-robed priest.  $93After the rite, brother,$94 the priest said, $93if you have gold I shall gladly attend to your mother.  Milord has bidden all clerics attend-and I, for one, have no wish to offend him.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93My mother's desperately ill,$94 Symmachus pled.  $93Surely Milord will not miss one lowly priest.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93True, but the Archcanon will,$94 the priest said nervously, tearing his robe loose from Symmachus' desperate grip and vanishing into the crowd.  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus tried other priests, and even a few mages, but with no better result.  Armored guards marched through the street and pushed him aside with their lances, and Symmachus realized that the royal procession was approaching.  <BR>
<BR>
As the carriage bearing the city's rulers drew abreast, Symmachus rushed out from the crowd and shouted, $93Milord, Milord!  My mother's dying-!$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93I forbid her to do so on this glorious night!$94 the Lord shouted, laughing and scattering coin into the throng.  Symmachus was close enough to smell wine on the royal breath.  On the other side of the carriage his Lady clutched the babe to her breast, and stared slit-eyed at Symmachus, her nostrils flared in disdain.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Guards!$94 she cried.  $93Remove this oaf.$94  Rough hands seized Symmachus.  He was beaten and left dazed by the side of the road.  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus, head aching, followed in the wake of the crowd and witnessed the Rite of Naming from the top of a hill.  He could see the brown-robed clerics and blue-robed mages gathered near the highborn folk far below.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah.  <BR>
<BR>
The name came dimly to Symmachus' ears as the High Priest lifted the swaddled babe and proffered her to the twin moons on either side of the horizon: Jone rising, Jode setting.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Behold the Lady Barenziah, born to the land of Mournhold!  Grant her thy blessings and thy counsel, ye kind gods, that she may ever rule well over Mournhold, its ken and its weal, its kith and its ilk.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Bless her, bless her,$94 all the people intoned along with their Lord and Lady, hands upraised.  <BR>
<BR>
Only Symmachus stood silent, head bowed, knowing in his heart that his dear mother was gone.  And in silence he swore a mighty oath-that he should be his Lord's bane, and in vengeance for his mother's needless death, the child Barenziah he should have for his own bride, and that his mother's grandchildren should be born to rule over Mournhold.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
After the ceremony, he watched impassively as the royal procession returned to the palace.  He saw the priest to whom he'd first spoken.  The man came gladly enough now in return for the gold Sym$ADmachus had, and a promise of more afterward.  <BR>
<BR>
They found his mother dead.  <BR>
<BR>
The priest sighed and tucked the pouch of gold coins away.  $93I'm sorry, brother.  It's all right, you can forget the rest of the gold, there's aught I can do here.  Likely-$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Give me back my money!$94 Symmachus snarled.  $93You've done naught to earn it!$94  He lifted his right arm threateningly.  <BR>
<BR>
The priest backed away, about to utter a curse, but Symmachus struck him across the face before more than three words had left his mouth.  He went down heavily, striking his head sharply on one of the stones that formed the fire pit.  He died instantly.  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus snatched up the gold and fled the city.  As he ran, he muttered one word over and over, like a sorcerer's chant.  $93Barenziah,$94 he said.  $93Barenziah.  Barenziah.$94  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Barenziah stood on one of the balconies of the palace, staring down into the courtyard where soldiers milled, dazzling in their armor.  Presently they formed into ordered ranks and cheered as her parents, the Lord and Lady, emerged from the palace, clad from head to toe in ebony armor, long purple-dyed fur cloaks flowing behind.  Splendidly caparisoned, shining black horses were brought for them, and they mounted and rode to the courtyard gates, and turned to salute her.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Barenziah!$94 they cried. $93Barenziah our beloved, farewell!$94  <BR>
<BR>
The little girl blinked back tears and waved one hand bravely, her favorite stuffed animal, a gray wolf$ADcub she called Wuffen, clutched to her breast with the other.  She had never been parted from her parents before and had no idea what it meant, save that there was war in the west and the name Tiber Septim was on everyone's lips, spoken in hate and dread.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Barenziah!$94 the soldiers cried, lifting their lances and swords and bows.  Then her dear parents turned and rode away, knights trailing in their wake, until the courtyard was nearly emptied.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Sometime after came a day when Barenziah was shaken awake by her nurse, dressed hurriedly, and borne from the palace.  <BR>
<BR>
All she could remember of that dreadful time was seeing a huge shadow with burning eyes filling the sky.  She was passed from hand to hand.  Foreign soldiers appeared, disappeared, and sometimes reappeared.  Her nurse vanished and was replaced by strangers, some more strange than others.  There were days, or it may have been weeks, of travel.  <BR>
<BR>
One morning she awoke to step out of the coach into a cold place with a large gray stone castle amid empty, endless gray-green hills covered patchily with gray-white snow.  She clutched Wuffen to her breast in both hands and stood blinking and shivering in the gray dawn, feeling very small and very dark in all this endless space, this endless gray-white space.  <BR>
<BR>
She and Hana, a brown-skinned, black-haired maid who had been traveling with her for several days, went inside the keep.  A large gray-white woman with icy gray-golden hair was standing by a hearth in one of the rooms.  She stared at Barenziah with dreadful, bright blue eyes.  <BR>
<BR>
$93She's very -- black, isn't she?$94 the woman remarked to Hana.  $93I've never seen a Dark Elf before.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93I don't know much about them myself, Milady,$94 Hana said.  $93But this one's got red hair and a temper to match, I can tell you that.  Take care.  She bites.  And worse.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93I'll soon train her out of that,$94 the other woman sniffed.  $93And what's that filthy thing she's got?  Ugh!$94  The woman snatched Wuffen away and threw him into the blazing hearth.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah shrieked and would have flung herself after him, but was held back despite her attempts to bite and claw at her captors.  Poor Wuffen was reduced to a tiny heap of charred ash.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Barenziah grew like a weed transplanted to a Skyrim garden, a ward of Count Sven and his wife the Lady Inga.  Outwardly, that is, she thrived -- but always there was a cold and empty place within.  <BR>
<BR>
$93I've raised her as my own daughter,$94 Lady Inga was wont to sigh as she sat gossiping when neighbor$ADing ladies came to visit.  $93But she's a Dark Elf.  What can you expect?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah was not meant to overhear these words.  At least she thought she was not.  Her hearing was keener than that of her Nordic hosts.  Other, less desirable Dark Elven traits evidently included pilfering, lying, and a little misplaced magic, just a small fire spell here and a little levitation spell there.  And, as she grew older, a keen interest in boys and men, who could provide very pleasant sensations -- and to her aston$ADishment, gifts as well.  Inga disapproved of this last for reasons incomprehensible to Barenziah, so she was careful to keep it as secret as possible.  <BR>
<BR>
$93She's wonderful with the children,$94 Inga added, referring to her five sons, all younger than Barenziah.  $93I don't think she'd ever let them come to harm.$94  A tutor had been hired when Jonni was six and Barenziah eight, and they took their lessons together.  She would have liked to train in arms as well, but the very idea scandalized Count Sven and Lady Inga.  So Barenziah was given a small bow and allowed to play at target shooting with the boys.  She watched them at arms practice when she could, sparred with them when no grownup folk were about, and knew she was good as or better than they.  <BR>
<BR>
$93She's very... proud, though, isn't she?$94 one of the ladies would whisper to Inga; and Barenziah, pre$ADtending not to hear, would nod silently in agreement.  She could not help but feel superior to the Count and his Lady.  There was something about them that provoked contempt.  <BR>
<BR>
Afterward she came to learn that Sven and Inga were distant cousins of Darkmoor Keep's last titled residents, and she finally understood.  They were poseurs, impostors, not rulers at all.  At least, they were not raised to rule.  This thought made her strangely furious at them, a good clean hatred quite detached from resentment.  She came to see them as disgusting and repellent insects who could be despised but never feared.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Once a month a courier came from the Emperor, bringing a small bag of gold for Sven and Inga and a large bag of dried mushrooms from Morrowind for Barenziah, her favorite treat.  On these occa$ADsions, she was always made to look presentable-or at least as presentable as a skinny Dark Elf could be made to look in Inga's eyes-before being summoned into the courier's presence for a brief interview.  The same courier seldom came twice, but all of them looked her over in much the same way a farmer would look over a hog he is readying for market.  <BR>
<BR>
In the spring of her sixteenth year, Barenziah thought the courier looked as if she were at last ready for market.  <BR>
<BR>
Upon reflection, she decided she did not wish to be marketed.  The stable-boy, Straw, a big, muscular blond lad, clumsy, gentle, affectionate, and rather simple, had been urging her to run off for some weeks now.  Barenziah stole the bag of gold the courier had left, took the mushrooms from the storeroom, dis$ADguised herself as a boy in one of Jonni's old tunics and a pair of his cast-off breeches... and on one fine spring night she and Straw took the two best horses from the stable and rode hard through the night toward Whiterun, the nearest city of any importance and the place where Straw wanted to be.  But Mournhold and Morrowind also lay eastward and they drew Barenziah as a lodestone draws iron.  <BR>
<BR>
In the morning they abandoned the horses at Barenziah's insistence.  She knew they would be missed and tracked down, and she hoped to throw off any pursuers.  <BR>
<BR>
They continued on foot until late afternoon, keeping to side roads, and slept for several hours in an abandoned hut.  They went on at dusk and came to Whiterun's city gates just before dawn.  Barenziah had prepared a pass of sorts for Straw, a makeshift document stating an errand to a temple in the city for a local village lord.  She herself glided over the wall with the help of a levitation spell.  She had reasoned-correctly, as it turned out-that by now the gate guards would have been alerted to keep an eye out for a young Dark Elven girl and a Nordic boy traveling together.  On the other hand, unaccompanied country yokels like Straw were a common enough sight.  Alone and with papers, it was unlikely that he would draw attention.  <BR>
<BR>
Her simple plan went smoothly.  She met Straw at the temple, which was not far from the gate; she had been to Whiterun on a few previous occasions.  Straw, however, had never been more than a few miles from Sven's estate, which was his birthplace.  <BR>
<BR>
Together they made their way to a rundown inn in the poorer quarters of Whiterun.  Gloved, cloaked, and hooded against the morning chill, Barenziah's dark skin and red eyes were not apparent and no one paid any heed to them.  They entered the inn separately.  Straw paid the innkeeper for a single cubicle, an immense meal, and two jugs of ale.  Barenziah sneaked in a few minutes later.  <BR>
<BR>
They ate and drank together gleefully, rejoicing in their escape, and made love vigorously on the narrow cot.  Afterward they fell into an exhausted, dreamless sleep.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
They stayed for a week at Whiterun.  Straw earned a bit of money running errands and Barenziah burgled a few houses at night.  She continued to dress as a boy.  She cut her hair short and dyed her flame-red tresses jet black to further the disguise, and kept out of sight as much as possible.  There were few Dark Elves in Whiterun.  <BR>
<BR>
One day Straw got them work as temporary guards for a merchant caravan traveling east.  The one-armed sergeant looked her over dubiously.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Heh,$94 he chuckled, $93Dark Elf, ain'tcha?  Like settin' a wolf t'guard the sheep, that is.  Still, I need arms, and we ain't goin' near 'nough Morrowind so's ye can betray us to yer folk.  Our homegrown bandits would as fain cut yer throat as mine.$94  <BR>
<BR>
The sergeant turned to give Straw an appraising look.  Then he spun back abruptly toward Barenziah, whipping out his shortsword.  But she had her dagger out in the twinkling of an eye and was in a defensive stance.  Straw drew his own knife and circled round to the man's rear.  The sergeant dropped his blade and chuckled again.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Not bad, kids, not bad.  How are ye with yon bow, Dark Elf?$94  Barenziah demonstrated her prowess briefly.  $93Aye, not bad, not bad 'tall.  And ye'll be keen of eye by night, boy, and of hearin' 'tall times.  A trusty Dark Elf makes as good a fightin' man as any could ask for.  I know.  I served under Symmachus his$ADself afore I lost this arm and got invalided outter the Emp'ror's army.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93We could betray them.  I know folk who'd pay well,$94 Straw said later as they bedded down for their last night at the ramshackle lodge.  $93Or rob them ourselves.  They're very rich, those merchants are, Berry.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah laughed.  $93Whatever would we do with so much money?  And besides, we need their protec$ADtion for traveling quite as much as they need ours.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93We could buy a little farm, you and me, Berry -- and settle down, all nice like.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Peasant! Barenziah thought scornfully.  Straw was a peasant and harbored nothing but peasant dreams.  But all she said was, $93Not here, Straw, we're too close to Darkmoor still.  We'll have other chances farther east.$94  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
The caravan went only as far east as Sunguard.  The Emperor Tiber Septim I had done much in the way of building relatively safe and regularly patrolled highways.  But the tolls were steep, and this par$ADticular caravan kept to the side roads as much as possible to avoid them.  This exposed them to the hazards of wayside robbers, both human and Orcish, and roving brigand bands of various races.  But such were the perils of trade and profit.  <BR>
<BR>
They had two such encounters before reaching Sunguard -- an ambush which Barenziah's keen ears warned them of in plenty of time for them to circle about and surprise the lurkers, and a night attack by a mixed band of Khajiit, humans, and Wood Elves.  The latter were a skilled band and even Barenziah did not hear them sneaking up in time to give much warning.  This time the fighting was fierce.  The attackers were driven off, but two of the caravan's other guards were slain and Straw got a nasty cut on his thigh before he and Barenziah managed to gash his Khajiit assailant's throat.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah rather enjoyed the life.  The garrulous sergeant had taken a liking to her, and she spent most of her evenings sitting around the campfire listening to his tales of campaigning in Morrowind with Tiber Septim and General Symmachus.  This Symmachus had been made general after Mournhold fell, the sergeant said.  $93He's a fine soldier, boy, Symmachus is.  But there was more'n soldiery involved'n that Morrowind business, if y'take my meanin'.  But, well, y'know all 'bout that, I 'spect.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93No.  No, I don't remember,$94 Barenziah said, trying to sound nonchalant.  $93I've lived most of my life in Skyrim.  My mother married a Skyrim man.  They're both dead, though.  Tell me, what happened to the Lord and Lady of Mournhold?$94  <BR>
<BR>
The sergeant shrugged.  $93I ain't never heard.  Dead, I 'spect. 'Twas alot of fightin' afore the Armistice got signed.  It's pretty quiet now.  Maybe too quiet.  Like a calm afore a storm.  Say, boy, you goin' back there?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Maybe,$94 Barenziah said.  The truth was that she was drawn irresistibly to Morrowind, and Mournhold, like a moth to a burning house.  Straw sensed it and was unhappy about it.  He was unhappy anyway since they could not bed together, as she was supposed to be a boy.  Barenziah rather missed it too, but not as much as Straw did, seemingly.  <BR>
<BR>
The sergeant wanted them to sign on for the return trip, but gave them a bonus nonetheless when they turned the offer down, and parchments of recommendation.  <BR>
<BR>
Straw wanted to settle down permanently near Sunguard, but Barenziah insisted on continuing their travels east.  $93I'm the Queen of Mournhold by rights,$94 she said, unsure whether it was true -- or was it just a daydream she had made up as a lost, bewildered child?  $93I want to go home.  I need to go home.$94  That at least was true.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
After a few weeks they managed to get places in another caravan heading east.  By early winter they were at Rifton, and nearing the Morrowind border.  But the weather had grown severe as the days passed and they were told no merchant caravans would be setting forth till mid-spring.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah stood on top of the city walls and stared across the deep gorge that separated Rifton from the snow-clad mountain wall guarding Morrowind beyond.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Berry,$94 Straw said gently.  $93Mournhold's a long way off yet, nearly as far as we've come already.  And the lands between are wild, full of wolves and bandits and Orcs and still worse creatures.  We'll have to wait for spring.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93There's Silgrod Tower,$94 Berry said, referring to the Dark Elven township that had grown up around an ancient minaret guarding the border between Skyrim and Morrowind.  <BR>
<BR>
$93The bridge guards won't let me across, Berry.  They're crack Imperial troops.  They can't be bribed.  If you go, you go alone.  I won't try and stop you.  But what will you do?  Silgrod Tower is full of Imperial sol$ADdiers.  Will you become a washing-woman for them?  Or a camp follower?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93No,$94 Barenziah said slowly, thoughtfully.  Actually the idea was not entirely unappealing.  She was sure she could earn a modest living by sleeping with the soldiers.  She'd had a few adventures of that sort as they crossed Skyrim, when she'd dressed as a woman and slipped away from Straw.  She'd only been looking for a bit of variety.  Straw was sweet but dull.  She'd been startled, but extremely pleased, when the men she picked up offered her money afterward.  Straw had been unhappy about it, though, and would shout for a while then sulk for days afterward if he caught her at it.  He was quite jealous.  He'd even threat$ADened to leave her.  Not that he ever did.  Or could.  <BR>
<BR>
But the Imperial Guards were a tough and brutal lot by all accounts, and Barenziah had heard some very ugly stories during their treks.  The ugliest of them by far had come from the lips of ex-army veterans around the caravan campfire, and were proudly recounted.  They'd been trying to shock her and Straw, she realized-but she also comprehended that there was some truth behind the wild tales.  Straw hated that kind of dirty talk, and hated it more that she had to hear it.  But there was a part of him that was fascinated never$ADtheless.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah sensed this and had encouraged Straw to seek out other women.  But he said he didn't want anyone else but her.  She told him candidly she didn't feel that way about him, but she did like him better than anyone else.  $93Then why do you go with other men?$94 Straw had asked on one occasion.  <BR>
<BR>
$93I don't know.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Straw sighed.  $93They say Dark Elven women are like that.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah smiled and shrugged.  $93I don't know.  Or, no ... maybe I do.  Yes, I do know.$94  She turned and kissed him affectionately.  $93I guess that's all the explanation there is.$94<BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
真实的巴兰兹娅·卷一<BR>
匿名　著<BR><BR>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><BR><BR>
五百年前，在哀伤之城的宝石之都，住着个盲寡妇和她唯一的孩子，一位身材高大、魁梧的年轻人。他是一名矿工，之前他的父亲也是一名矿工，在哀伤之城的矿场里做普通工人，因他的魔法才能很小。这项工作是光荣的，但报酬很低。他的母亲在城市市场制作和出售异梅蛋糕以维持生计。她说，他们做得很好，他们有足够的东西填饱肚子，没人能一次穿多套衣服，而且屋顶只在下雨时才会漏水。但塞马库斯想要更多。他希望能在矿里碰碰运气，为他带来丰厚的奖金。在空闲时刻，他喜欢和朋友们在小酒馆里小酌啤酒，和他们一起赌牌。他还吸引了不止一位漂亮精灵姑娘的目光与叹息，尽管没人能长久地引起他的兴趣。他是典型的农民出身的年轻暗精灵，仅凭他的体型就可圈可点。传闻他身上带点诺德血统。<BR>
<BR>
塞马库斯三十岁时，哀伤之城一阵欢腾——君王和夫人生下了一位女孩。女王，人们欢唱，为我们而生的女王！因为在哀伤之城的人们中，女继承人的诞生是未来和平与繁荣的必然标志。<BR>
<BR>
当王室之子的命名仪式时刻已到，矿场关闭了，塞马库斯冲回家洗澡，穿上他最好的衣服。“我会直接回家告诉你这一切，”他向他的母亲保证，她不能参加。她一直病着，而且还会有一大群人，因为所有的哀伤之城都变成了幸福的一部分；而且她是盲人，无论如何她什么都看不见。<BR>
<BR>
“我的儿，”她说。“你走之前，给我找个牧师或者治疗师吧，不然你回来之前我可能已撒手人寰。”<BR>
<BR>
塞马库斯立刻走到她的床前，焦急地注意到她的前额很烫，呼吸很浅。他撬开一块木地板，地板下面放着他们的小积蓄。几乎没有足够的钱以支付牧师的治疗费用。他不得不倾其所有，其余的先欠着。塞马库斯抓起他的斗篷，匆匆离开。<BR>
<BR>
街道上挤满了赶往圣石的人们，但神殿却被锁上了。“因仪式闭馆”，他读着所有的标语。<BR>
<BR>
塞马库斯从人群中挤过，成功追上了一名棕袍牧师。“仪式结束后，兄弟，”牧师说着，“如果你有金子，我会很乐意照顾你的母亲。君王大人已请所有神职人员出席——我，其中之一，不想冒犯他。”<BR>
<BR>
“我母亲病得很重，”塞马库斯恳求道。“想必大人不会在意任何一个卑微的牧师。”<BR>
<BR>
“说的很对，但大主教会。”牧师紧张地说着，从塞马库斯绝望的手中扯下他的长袍，消失在了人群中。<BR>
<BR>
塞马库斯尝试了其他牧师，甚至是一些法师，但没有更好的结果。武装卫兵穿过街道，用长矛将他推到一边，塞马库斯意识到皇家列队正在逼近。<BR>
<BR>

***<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹娅长得像一缕移植到天际花园的杂草，斯文和他的妻子英加夫人为其监护人。表面上，也就是说，她茁壮成长——但内心总是有一个寒冷而空虚的地方。<BR>
<BR>
“我把她当成自己的女儿养大了，”当邻居女士来访时，英加夫人坐着闲聊，她习惯性地叹息。“但她是个暗精灵。你能期待什么？”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹娅不是故意听到这些话的。至少她认为她不是。她的听力比她的诺德主人还要敏锐。其他较不受欢迎的暗精灵特征显然包括盗窃、撒谎和一些放错地方的魔法，这里只有个火花咒，那里又有个小浮空咒。而且，随着年龄的增长，她对男孩和男人产生了浓厚的兴趣，令她惊讶的是——他们可以提供非常愉快的感觉，还有礼物。由于巴兰兹娅无法理解的原因，英加不赞成最后一个，所以她小心翼翼地尽可能保密。<BR>
<BR>
“她和孩子们相处得很好，”英加补充说，指的是她的五个儿子，都比巴兰兹娅小。“我认为她不会让他们受到伤害。”乔尼六岁、巴兰兹娅八岁的时候聘请了一位导师，他们一起上课。她本来也想接受武器训练，但这个想法让斯文伯爵和英加夫人感到震惊。因此，巴兰兹娅得到了一张小弓，并被允许与男孩们一起玩靶子射术。她尽可能地看着他们练习武器，在没有大人在场的时候和他们对打，并且知道她和他们一样好，或者比他们好。<BR>
<BR>
“不过，她很……很自豪，不是吗？”其中一位女士会对英加耳语；而巴兰兹娅则装作没听见，默默点头表示同意。她不禁觉得自己比伯爵和他的夫人高人一等。他们身上有些东西引起了人们的鄙视。<BR>
<BR>
后来她得知斯文和英加是暗沼要塞(Darkmoor Keep)最后一位有名居民的远房表亲，她终于明白了。他们是装腔作势者，冒名顶替者，根本不是统治者。至少，他们没有被升格为统治者。这个想法使她对他们感到奇怪的愤怒，一种与怨恨完全分离干净的仇恨。她开始将它们视为令人厌恶和排斥的昆虫，可以被鄙视但从不令人害怕。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
每月一次，皇帝送来一个信使，给斯文和英加带来一小袋金子，给巴兰兹娅带来一大袋晨风干蘑菇，这是巴兰兹娅的最爱。在这些场合，她总是被要求看起来像样——或者至少在被召唤到信使面前进行简短采访之前，她看起来就像一个瘦弱的暗精灵看着英加的眼睛。同一个信使很少来两次，但他们都像农民看着准备上市的猪一样看着她。<BR>
<BR>
在她十六岁那年的春天，巴兰兹娅认为信使看她好像终于准备好上市了。<BR>
<BR>
经过反思，她决定不希望被推销。马厩男孩斯特劳，一个身材高大、肌肉发达的金发小伙子，笨拙、温柔、深情，而且思维质朴，几个星期以来一直在敦促她逃跑。巴兰兹娅偷走了信使留下的一袋金子，从储藏室拿走了蘑菇，把自己伪装成一个男孩，穿着乔尼的一件旧长袍和一条废弃的马裤……在一个晴朗的春夜她和斯特劳从马厩里带走了两匹最好的马，彻夜驱马向白漫城驶去，这是离得最近的重要城市，也是斯特劳想去的地方。但哀伤之城和晨风也在东方，他们吸引着巴兰兹娅，就像一块磁石吸引着铁一样。<BR>
<BR>
早上，在巴兰兹娅的坚持下，他们放弃了马匹。她知道它们会被遗漏并被追踪，她希望赶走任何追捕者。<BR>
<BR>
他们一直步行到下午晚些时候，一直走在小路上，在一个废弃的小屋里睡了几个小时。他们在黄昏前行，在黎明前来到了白漫的城门。巴兰兹娅为斯特劳准备了一张通行证，一份临时文件，上面写着为当地的村主去城里的一座神殿跑腿。她自己在浮空咒语的帮助下滑过墙壁。她的推理——事实证明是正确的——到现在为止，门卫已经被提醒注意一个年轻的暗精灵女孩和一个诺德男孩一起旅行。另一方面，像斯特劳这样无人陪伴的乡下人却很常见。独自一人和持有文件，他不太可能引起注意。<BR>
<BR>
她简单的计划进行得很顺利。她在离大门不远的神殿遇见了斯特劳。她以前去过几次白漫。然而，斯特劳离他的出生地斯文庄园从未超过几英里。<BR>
<BR>
他们一起前往白漫较贫困地区的一家破旧旅馆。戴着手套，披着斗篷，戴着兜帽抵挡着清晨的寒意，巴兰兹娅的黑皮肤和红眼睛并不明显，没有人在意。他们分别进了客栈。斯特劳付给旅店老板些钱，得到了一个小隔间、一顿丰盛的饭菜和两罐啤酒。几分钟后，巴兰兹娅偷偷潜入。<BR>
<BR>
他们兴高采烈地吃喝，为逃脱而欣喜若狂，在狭窄的小床上热烈地做爱。之后，他们陷入了疲惫而无梦的睡眠中。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
他们在白漫住了一个星期。斯特劳跑腿赚了点钱，巴兰兹娅晚上偷了几间房子。她继续打扮得像个男孩。她剪短了头发，将火红色的头发染成了乌黑，以进一步掩饰，尽可能地远离视线。白漫城的暗精灵很少。<BR>
<BR>
有一天，斯特劳让他们担任东行商队的临时警卫。独臂中士疑惑地看了她一眼。<BR>
<BR>
“呵呵，”他轻笑道，“暗精灵，不是吗？就像在羊群中设置狼卫兵一样。不过，我需要武器，我们不能靠近‘晨风’，所以你们可以把我们出卖给你们的人。我们土生土长的土匪会像我一样想割断你的喉咙。”<BR>
<BR>
中士转身给斯特劳一个评估的眼神。然后他猛地回身，朝着巴兰兹娅挥出短剑。可她一眨眼的功夫就拔出匕首，摆出防御的姿势。斯特劳拔出自己的刀，绕到男人的身后。中士放下刀刃，再次轻笑起来。<BR>
<BR>
“不错，孩子们，真不错。暗精灵，你的弓术怎么样？”巴兰兹娅短暂地展示了她的实力。“是的，不赖，真不赖，个头也不错。孩子，你晚上会很敏锐，很想听很久。一个值得信赖的暗精灵会成为一个好斗的人，任何人都可以要求。我知道。在失去这条手臂并在皇帝的军队之外失去能力之前，我曾在塞马库斯手下服役。”<BR>
<BR>
“我们可以背叛他们。我认识愿意付高价的人，”斯特劳后来说，他们在摇摇欲坠的小屋里睡了最后一晚。“或者我们自己去抢劫他们。他们很富有，那些商人，贝瑞。”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹娅笑道。“我们拿这么多钱做什么？此外，我们在旅行中需要他们的保护，就像他们需要我们的一样。”<BR>
<BR>
“我们可以买一个小农场，你和我，贝瑞——然后安顿下来，一切安好。”<BR>
<BR>
农夫！巴兰兹娅轻蔑地想。斯特劳是个农民，除了农民的梦想什么也没有。但她只是说，“不在这里，斯特劳，我们离暗沼太近了。我们将在更远的东部有其他机会。”<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
商队只到了阳卫城（Sungard）的东边。泰伯·塞普汀一世皇帝在建造相对安全且定期巡逻的公路方面做了很多工作。但是过路费很高，这支特殊的大篷车尽可能地保持在小路上以避免它们。这使他们暴露在路边强盗的危险中，包括人类和兽人，以及各个种族的流动强盗团伙。但这就是贸易和利润的危险。<BR>
<BR>
他们在到达阳卫之前遇到了两次这样的遭遇——一次是巴兰兹娅敏锐的耳朵，在充足的时间警告他们的伏击，让他们在周围盘旋并突袭潜伏者，由卡吉特混合队伍发起的夜间袭击，人类，还有木精灵。后者是一支技术娴熟的队伍，连巴兰兹娅都没有及时听到他们偷偷摸摸，发出警告。这一次的战斗非常激烈。袭击者被赶走，但商队的另外两名警卫被杀，斯特劳的大腿被严重割伤，随后他和巴兰兹娅设法割开了袭击者卡吉特的喉咙。<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹娅相当享受生活。喋喋不休的中士很喜欢她，她晚上大部分时间都坐在营火旁，听他讲述他在晨风中与泰伯·塞普汀和塞马库斯将军一起作战的故事。“哀伤之城沦陷后，这位塞马库斯被任命为将军。”中士说道。“他是位优秀的士兵，孩子，塞马库斯。但是，如果你听懂我的意思，那晨风的事讲牵涉到更多的优秀‘军人’。但是，好吧，你知道这一切，我猜。”<BR>
<BR>
“不。不，我不记得了，”巴兰兹娅努力装出一副若无其事的样子。“我一生中的大部分时间都在天际度过。我妈妈嫁给了一个天际男人。不过，他们都死了。告诉我，哀伤之城的王和他夫人怎么了？”<BR>
<BR>
中士耸了耸肩。“我没听说过。死了吧，我猜。在停战协议签署之前，‘打了很多仗’。现在很安静。也许太安静了。就像暴风雨前的宁静。话说，小子，你要回去吗？”<BR>
<BR>
“也许吧，”巴兰兹娅说道。原来，她对晨风和哀伤之城情有独钟，就像飞蛾扑火一样。斯特劳察觉到了，对此感到不高兴。反正他很不开心，因为他们不能睡在一起，因为她应该是个男孩。巴兰兹娅也很想念它，但似乎没有斯特劳那么想念。<BR>
<BR>
中士希望他们在回程时签约，但当他们拒绝了提议时，还是给了他们奖金和推荐信。<BR>
<BR>
斯特劳想在阳卫附近永久定居，但巴兰兹娅坚持要继续向东旅行。“按理说，我是哀伤之城的女王。”她说，不确定这是否属实——还是她作为一个迷失迷惘的孩子编造的白日梦？“我想回家。我得回家了。”至少这是真的。<BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
几周后，他们设法在另一个向东行驶的大篷车中找到了位置。到了初冬，他们到达了裂谷城，接近了晨风边界。但是随着时间的流逝，天气变得越来越恶劣，他们被告知在仲春之前不会有商队出发。<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹娅站在城墙之上，凝视着隔开裂谷与守护晨风的白雪皑皑的山墙之间的幽深峡谷。<BR>
<BR>
“贝瑞，”斯特劳温和地说。“哀伤之城还很远，就跟我们来时差不多。中间的土地荒芜，到处都是狼、强盗、兽人，还有更糟糕的生物。我们将不得不等待春天。”<BR>
<BR>
“这里是希尔格罗德塔(Silgrod Tower)。”贝瑞指的是暗精灵小镇，它围绕着一个古老的尖塔，守卫着天际和晨风的边界。<BR>
<BR>
“守桥人不让我过去，贝瑞。他们是精锐的帝国军队。他们不能被贿赂。如果你去，你一个人去。我不会试图阻止你。但是你会怎么做？希尔格罗德塔到处都是帝国的士兵。你会成为他们的‘洗衣妇’吗？还是‘营地追随者’？”<BR>
<BR>
“不，”巴兰兹娅若有所思地缓缓说道。事实上，这个想法并非完全没有吸引力。她确信她可以通过和士兵陪睡来过上微薄的生活。当她穿得像女人一样从斯特劳身边溜走时，她经历过几次类似的冒险。她只是在寻找一些变化。斯特劳很甜腻但很乏味。当她见到的男人后来给她钱时，她吃了一惊，但非常高兴。不过，斯特劳对此很不高兴，如果他抓住她，他会大喊大叫，然后闷闷不乐好几天。他非常嫉妒。他甚至威胁要离开她。他从来没有这样做过。或者可以。<BR>
<BR>
但帝国的近卫军，历来都是强悍而残暴的，巴兰兹娅在跋涉的过程中，也听过一些非常丑陋的故事。迄今为止，最丑陋的来自商队营火周围的退伍老兵之口，并被自豪地讲述了一遍。他们一直在震惊她和斯特劳，她意识到——但她也明白这些荒唐的故事背后有一些真相。斯特劳讨厌那种脏话，更讨厌她不得不听。但是，他的一部分仍然被迷住了。<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹娅察觉到这一点，鼓励斯特劳去寻找其他女性。但他说，除了她，他不想要任何人。她坦率地告诉他，她对他没有那种感觉，但她确实比任何人都更喜欢他。“那你为什么要跟别的男人走？”斯特劳曾经问过一次。<BR>
<BR>
“我不知道。”<BR>
<BR>
斯特劳叹了口气。“他们说，暗精灵女人就是这样。”<BR>
<BR>
巴兰兹娅微笑着耸了耸肩。“我不知道。或者，不……也许我知道。是的，我知道。”她转身，深情地吻了他。“我想这就是所有的解释。”<BR>

As Symmachus had predicted, the theft of the Staff of Chaos had few short-term consequences.  The current Emperor, Uriel Septim, sent some rather stiff messages expressing shock and displeasure at the Staff's disappearance, and urging Symmachus to make every effort to locate its whereabouts and communicate developments to the newly appointed Imperial Battlemage, Jagar Tharn, in whose hands the matter had been placed.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Tharn!$94 Symmachus thundered in disgust and frustration as he paced about the small chamber where Barenziah, now some months pregnant, was sitting serenely embroidering a baby blanket.  $93Jagar Tharn, indeed.  Ai!  I wouldn't give him directions for crossing the street, not if he were a doddering old blind sot.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93What have you against him, love?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93I just don't trust that mongrel Elf.  Part Dark Elf, part High Elf, and part the gods only know what.  All the worst qualities of all his combined bloods, I'll warrant.$94  He snorted.  $93No one knows much about him.  Claims he was born in southern Valenwood, of a Wood Elven mother.  Seems to have been everywhere since -- $94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah, sunk in the contentment and lassitude of pregnancy, had only been humoring Symmachus thus far.  But now she suddenly dropped her needlework and looked at him.  Something had piqued her interest.  $93Symmachus.  Could this Jagar Tharn have been the Nightingale, disguised?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus thought this over before replying.  $93Nay, my love.  Human blood seems to be the one missing component in Tharn's ancestry.$94  To Symmachus, Barenziah knew, that was a flaw.  Her husband despised Wood Elves as lazy thieves and High Elves as effete intellectuals.  But he admired humans, especially Bretons, for their combination of pragmatism, intelligence, and energy.  $93The Nightingale's of Ebonheart, of the Ra'athim Clan - House Hlaalu, the House of Mora in particular, I'll be bound.  That house has had human blood in it since her time.  Ebonheart was jealous that the Staff was laid here when Tiber Septim took the Horn of Summoning from us.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah sighed a little.  The rivalry between Ebonheart and Mournhold reached back almost to the dawn of Morrowind's history.  Once the two nations had been one, all the lucrative mines held in fief by the Ra'athims, whose nobility retained the High Kingship of Morrowind.  Ebonheart had split into two separate city-states, Ebonheart and Mournhold, when Queen Lian's twin sons -- grandsons of the legendary King Moraelyn -- were left as joint heirs.  At about the same time the office of High King was vacated in favor of a temporary War Leader to be named by a council in times of provincial emergency.  <BR>
<BR>
Still, Ebonheart remained jealous of her prerogatives as the eldest city-state of Morrowind ($93first among equals$94 was the phrase its rulers often quoted) and claimed that rightful guardianship of the Staff of Chaos should have been entrusted to its ruling house.  Mournhold responded that King Moraelyn himself had placed the Staff in the keeping of the god Ephen -- and Mournhold was unarguably the god's birthplace.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Why not tell Jagar Tharn of your suspicions, then?  Let him recover the thing.  As long as it's safe, what does it matter who recovers it, or where it lies?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus stared at her without comprehension.  $93It matters,$94 he said softly after a while, $93but I suppose not that much.  Ai.$94  He added, $93Certainly not enough for you to concern yourself further with it.  You just sit there and tend to your,$94 and here he smiled at her wickedly, $93embroidery.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah flung the sampler at him.  It hit Symmachus square in the face -- needle, thimble, and all.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
In a few more months Barenziah gave birth to a fine son, whom they named Helseth.  Nothing more was heard of the Staff of Chaos, or the Nightingale.  If Ebonheart had the Staff in its possession, they certainly did not boast of it.  <BR>
<BR>
The years passed swiftly and happily.  Helseth grew tall and strong.  He was much like his father, whom he worshipped.  When Helseth was eight years old Barenziah bore a second child, a daughter, to Symmachus' lasting delight.  Helseth was his pride, but little Morgiah -- named for Symmachus' mother -- held his heart.  <BR>
<BR>
Sadly, the birth of Morgiah was not the harbinger of better times ahead.  Relations with the Empire slowly deteriorated, for no apparent reason.  Taxes were raised and quotas increased with each passing year.  Symmachus felt that the Emperor suspected him of having had a hand in the Staff's disappearance and sought to prove his loyalty by making every effort to comply with the escalating demands.  He lengthened working hours and raised tariffs, and even made up some of the difference from both the royal exchequer and their own private holdings.  But the levies multiplied, and commoners and nobles alike began to complain.  It was an ominous rumble.  <BR>
<BR>
$93I want you to take the children and journey to the Imperial City,$94 Symmachus said at last in desperation one evening after dinner.  $93You must make the Emperor listen, else all Mournhold will be up in revolt come spring.$94  He grinned forcibly.  $93You have a way with men, love.  You always did.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah forced a smile of her own.  $93Even with you, I take it.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Yes.  Especially with me,$94 he acknowledged amiably.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Both children?$94  Barenziah looked over toward a corner window, where Helseth was strumming a lute and crooning a duet with his little sister.  Helseth was fifteen by then, Morgiah eight.  <BR>
<BR>
$93They might soften his heart.  Besides, it's high time Helseth was presented before the Imperial Court.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Perhaps.  But that's not your true reason.$94  Barenziah took a deep breath and grasped the nettle.  $93You don't think you can keep them safe here.  If that's the case, then you're not safe here either.  Come with us,$94 she urged.  <BR>
<BR>
He took her hands in his.  $93Barenziah.  My love.  Heart of my heart.  If I leave now, there'll be nothing for us to return to.  Don't worry about me.  I'll be all right.  Ai!  I can take care of myself -- and I can do it better if I'm not worrying about you or the children.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah laid her head against his chest.  $93Just remember that we need you.  I need you.  We can do without the rest of it if we have each other.  Empty hands and empty bellies are easier to bear than an empty heart.$94  She started to cry, thinking of the Nightingale and that sordid business with the Staff.  $93My foolishness has brought us to this pass.$94  <BR>
<BR>
He smiled at her tenderly.  $93If so, 'tis not so bad a place to be.$94  His eyes rested indulgently on their children.  $93None of us shall ever go without, or want for anything.  Ever.  Ever, my love, I promise you.  I cost you everything once, Barenziah, I and Tiber Septim.  Ai.  Without my aid the Empire would never have begun.  I helped its rise.$94  His voice hardened.  $93I can bring about its fall.  You may tell Uriel Septim that.  That, and that my patience is not infinite.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah gasped.  Symmachus was not given to empty threats.  She'd no more imagined that he would ever turn against the Empire than that the old house wolf lying by the grate would turn on her.  $93How?$94 she demanded breathlessly.  But he shook his head.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Better that you not know,$94 he said.  $93Just tell him what I told you should he prove recalcitrant, and do not fear.  He's Septim enough that he will not take it out on the messenger.$94  He smiled grimly.  $93For if he does, if he ever harms the least hair on you, my love, or the children -- so help me all the gods of Tamriel, he'll pray that he hadn't been born.  Ai.  I'll hunt him down, him and his entire family.  And I won't rest until the last Septim is dead.$94  The red Dark Elven eyes of Symmachus gleamed brightly in the ebbing firelight.  $93I plight you that oath, my love.  My Queen ... my Barenziah.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah held him, held him as tight as she could.  But in spite of the warmth in his embrace, she couldn't help shivering.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
Barenziah stood before the Emperor's throne, trying to explain Mournhold's straits.  She'd waited weeks for an audience with Uriel Septim, having been fobbed off on this pretext or that.  $93His Majesty is indisposed.$94  $93An urgent matter demands His Excellency's attention.$94  $93I am sorry, Your Highness, there must be some mistake.  Your appointment is for next week.  No, see...$94  And now it wasn't even going well.  The Emperor did not even make the slightest pretence at listening to her.  He hadn't invited her to sit, nor had he dismissed the children.  Helseth stood still as a carven image, but little Morgiah had begun to fuss.  <BR>
<BR>
The state of her own mind didn't help her any.  Shortly upon arrival at her lodgings, the Mournholdian ambassador to the Imperial City had demanded entry, bringing with him a sheaf of dispatches from Symmachus.  Bad news, and plenty of it.  The revolt had finally begun.  The peasants had organized around a few disgruntled members of Mournhold's minor nobility, and were demanding Symmachus step down and hand over the reins of government.  Only the Imperial Guard and a handful of troops whose families had been retainers of Barenziah's house for generations stood between Symmachus and the rabble.  Hostilities had already broken out, but apparently Symmachus was safe and still in control.  Not for long, he wrote.  He entreated Barenziah to try her best with the Emperor -- but in any case she was to stay in the Imperial City until he wrote to tell her it was safe to go back home with the children.  <BR>
<BR>
She had tried to barge her way through the Imperial bureaucracy -- with little success.  And to add to her growing panic, all news from Mournhold had come to a sudden stop.  Tottering between rage at the Emperor's numerous major-domos and fear of the fate awaiting her and her family, the weeks had passed by tensely, agonizingly, remorselessly.  Then one day the Mournholdian ambassador came calling to tell her she should expect news from Symmachus the following night at the latest, not through the regular channels but by nighthawk.  Seemingly by the same stroke of luck, she was informed that same day by a clerk from the Imperial Court that Uriel Septim had finally consented to grant her an audience early on the morrow.  <BR>
<BR>
The Emperor had greeted the three of them when they came into the audience chamber with a too-bright smile of welcome that nonetheless didn't reach his eyes.  Then, as she presented her children, he had gazed at them with a fixed attention that was real yet somehow inappropriate.  Barenziah had been dealing with humans for nearly five hundred years now, and had developed the skill of reading their expressions and movements that was far beyond what any human could ever perceive.  Try as the Emperor might to conceal it, there was hunger in his eyes -- and something else.  Regret?  Yes.  Regret.  But why?  He had several fine children of his own.  Why covet hers?  And why look at her with such a vicious -- however brief -- yearning?  Perhaps he had tired of his consort.  Humans were notoriously, though predictably, inconstant.  After that one long, burning glance, his gaze had shifted away as she began to speak of her mission and the violence that had erupted in Mournhold.  He sat still as stone throughout her entire account.  <BR>
<BR>
Puzzled at his inertia, and vexed no end, Barenziah stared into the pale, set face, looking for some trace of the Septims she'd known in the past.  She didn't know Uriel Septim well, having met him once when he was still a child, and then again at his coronation twenty years before.  Twice, that was all.  He'd been a stern and dignified presence at the ceremony, even as a young adult -- yet not icily remote as this more mature man was.  In fact, despite the physical resemblance, he didn't seem to be the same man at all.  Not the same, yet something about him was familiar to her, more familiar than it should be, some trick of posture or gesture...  <BR>
<BR>
Suddenly she felt very hot, as if lava had been poured over her.  Illusion!  She had studied the arts of illusion well since the Nightingale had deceived her so badly.  She had learned to detect it -- and she felt it now, as certainly as a blind man could feel the sun on his face.  Illusion!  But why?  Her mind worked furiously even as her mouth went on reciting details about Mournhold's troubles.  Vanity?  Humans were oft as ashamed at the signs of ageing as Elves were proud to exhibit them.  Yet the face Uriel Septim wore seemed consistent with his age.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah dared use none of her own magic.  Even petty nobles had means of detecting magicka, if not actually shielding themselves from its effects, within their own halls.  The use of sorcery here would bring down the Emperor's wrath as surely as drawing a dagger would.  <BR>
<BR>
Magic.  <BR>
<BR>
Illusion.  <BR>
<BR>
Suddenly she was brought to mind of the Nightingale.  And then he was sitting before her.  Then the vision changed, and it was Uriel Septim.  He looked sad.  Trapped.  And then the vision faded once more, and another man sat in his place, like the Nightingale, and yet unlike.  Pale skin, bloodshot eyes, Elven ears -- and about him a fierce glow of concentrated malice, an aura of eldritch energy -- a horrible, destructive shimmer.  This man was capable of anything!  <BR>
<BR>
And then once again she was looking into the face of Uriel Septim.  <BR>
<BR>
How could she be sure she wasn't imagining things?  Perhaps her mind was playing tricks on her.  She felt a sudden vast weariness, as if she'd been carrying a heavy burden too long and too far.  She decided to abandon her earnest narrative of Mournhold's ills -- as it was quite plainly getting her nowhere -- and switch back to pleasantry.  Pleasantry, however, with a hidden agenda.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Do you remember, Sire, Symmachus and I had dinner with your family shortly after your father's coronation?  You were no older than tiny Morgiah here.  We were greatly honored to be the only guests that evening -- except for your best friend Justin, of course.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Ah yes,$94 the Emperor said, smiling cautiously.  Very cautiously.  $93I do believe I recall that.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93You and Justin were such friends, Your Majesty.  I was told he died not long after.  A great pity.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Indeed.  I still do not like to speak of him.$94  His eyes turned blank -- or blanker, if it had been possible.  $93As for your request, Milady, we shall take it under advisement and let you know.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah bowed, as did the children.  A nod from the Emperor dismissed them, and they backed away from the imperial presence.  <BR>
<BR>
She took a deep breath when they emerged from the throne room.  $93Justin$94 had been an imaginary playmate, although young Uriel had insisted a place be set for Justin at every meal.  Not only that, Justin, despite the boyish name, had been a girl!  Symmachus had kept up the joke long after she had gone the way of imaginary childhood friends -- inquiring after Justin's health whenever he and Uriel Septim met, and being responded to in as mock-serious a fashion.  The last Barenziah had heard of Justin, several years ago, the Emperor had evidently joked elaborately to Symmachus that she had met an adventurous though incorrigible Khajiit youth, married him, and settled down in Lilandril to raise fire ferns and mugworts.  <BR>
<BR>
The man sitting on the Emperor's divan was not Uriel Septim!  The Nightingale?  Could it be...?  Yes.  Yes!  A chord of recognition rang through her and Barenziah knew she was right.  It was him.  It was!  The Nightingale!  Masquerading as the Emperor!  Symmachus had been wrong, so wrong...<BR>
<BR>
What now? she wondered frantically.  What had become of Uriel Septim -- and more to the point, what did it mean for her and Symmachus, and all of Mournhold?  Thinking back, Barenziah guessed that their troubles were due to this false Emperor, this Nightingale-spawned glamour -- or whatever he really was.  He must have taken Uriel Septim's place shortly before the unreasonable demands on Mournhold had begun.  That would explain why relations had deteriorated for so long (as humans reckoned time), long after her disapproved liaison with Tiber Septim.  The Nightingale knew of Symmachus' famed loyalty to, and knowledge of, the Septim House, and was effecting a pre-emptive strike.  If that were the case, they were all in terrible danger.  She and the children were in his power here in the Imperial City, and Symmachus was left alone to deal with troubles of the Nightingale's brewing in Mournhold.  <BR>
<BR>
What must she do?  Barenziah impelled the children ahead of her, a hand on each shoulder, trying to stay cool, collected, her ladies-in-waiting and personal knights escort trailing behind.  Finally they reached their waiting carriage.  Even though their suite of rooms was only a few blocks from the Palace, royal dignity forbade travel on foot for even short distances -- and for once, Barenziah was glad of it.  The carriage seemed a kind of refuge now, false as she knew the feeling must be.  <BR>
<BR>
A boy dashed up to one of the guards and handed him a scroll, then pointed toward the carriage.  The guard brought it to her.  The boy waited, eyes wide and shining.  The epistle was brief and complimentary, and simply inquired if King Eadwyre of Wayrest, of the Province of High Rock, might be granted an audience with the famed Queen Barenziah of Mournhold, as he had heard much of her and would be pleased to make her acquaintance.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah's first impulse was to refuse.  She wanted only to leave this city!  Certainly she had no inclination toward any dalliance with a dazzled human.  She looked up, frowning, and one of the guards said, $93Milady, the boy says his master awaits your reply yonder.$94  She looked in the direction indicated and saw a handsome elderly man on horseback, surrounded by a half dozen courtiers and cavaliers.  He caught her eye and bowed respectfully, taking off a plumed hat.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Very well,$94 Barenziah said to the boy on impulse.  $93Tell your master he may call on me tonight, after the dinner hour.$94  King Eadwyre looked polite and grave, and rather worried -- but not in the least lovestruck.  At least that was something, she thought pensively.  <BR>
Barenziah stood at the tower window, waiting.  She could sense the familiar's nearness.  But though the night sky was clear as day to her eyes, she could not yet see him.  Then suddenly he was there, a swift moving dot beneath the wispy night clouds.  A few more minutes and the great nighthawk finished its descent, wings folding, talons reaching for her thick leather armband.  <BR>
<BR>
She carried the bird to its perch, where it waited, panting, as her impatient fingers felt for the message secured in a capsule on one leg.  The hawk drank mightily from the water till when she had done, then ruffled its feathers and preened, secure in her presence.  A tiny part of her consciousness shared its satisfaction at a job well done, mission accomplished, and rest earned ... yet beneath it all was unease.  Things were not right, even to its humble avian mind.  <BR>
<BR>
Her fingers shook as she unfolded the thin parchment and pored over the cramped writing.  Not Symmachus' bold hand!  Barenziah sat slowly, fingers smoothing the document while she prepared her mind and body to accept disaster calmly, if disaster it would be.  <BR>
<BR>
Disaster it was.  <BR>
<BR>
The Imperial Guard had deserted Symmachus and joined the rebels.  Symmachus was dead.  The remaining loyal troops had suffered a decisive defeat.  Symmachus was dead.  The rebel leader had been recognized as King of Mournhold by Imperial envoys.  Symmachus was dead.  Barenziah and the children had been declared traitors to the Empire and a price set on their heads. <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus was dead.  <BR>
<BR>
So the audience with the Emperor earlier that morning had been nothing but a blind, a ruse.  A charade.  The Emperor must have already known.  She was just being strung along, told to stay put, take things easy, Milady Queen, enjoy the Imperial City and the delights it has to offer, do make your stay as long as you want.  Her stay?  Her detention.  Her captivity.  And in all probability, her impending arrest.  She had no delusions about her situation.  She knew the Emperor and his minions would never let her leave the Imperial City, ever again.  At least, not alive.  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus was dead.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Milady?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah jumped, startled by the servant's approach.  $93What is it?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93The Breton is here, Milady.  King Eadwyre,$94 the woman added helpfully, noting Barenziah's incomprehension.  She hesitated.  $93Is there news, Milady?$94 she said, nodding toward the nighthawk.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Nothing that will not wait,$94 Barenziah said quickly, and her voice seemed to echo in the emptiness that suddenly yawned like a gaping abyss inside her.  $93See to the bird.$94  She stood up, smoothed her gown, and prepared to attend on her royal visitor.  <BR>
<BR>
She felt numb.  Numb as the stone walls around her, numb as the quiescence of the night air... numb as a lifeless corpse.  <BR>
<BR>
Symmachus was dead!  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>

King Eadwyre greeted her gravely and courteously, if a bit fulsomely.  He claimed to be a fervent admirer of Symmachus, who figured prominently in his family's legends.  Gradually he turned the conversation to her business with the Emperor.  He inquired after details, and asked if the outcome had been favorable to Mournhold.  Finding her noncommittal, he suddenly blurted out, $93Milady Queen, you must believe me.  The man who claims himself the Emperor is an impostor!  I know it sounds mad, but I -- $94  <BR>
<BR>
$93No,$94 Barenziah said, with sudden decisiveness.  $93You are entirely correct, Milord King.  I know.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Eadwyre relaxed into his seat for the first time, eyes suddenly shrewd.  $93You know?  You're not just humoring someone you might think a madman?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93I assure you, Milord, I am not.$94  She took a deep breath.  $93And who do you surmise is dissembling as the Emperor?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93The Imperial Battlemage, Jagar Tharn.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Ah. Milord King, have you, perchance, heard of someone called the Nightingale?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Yes, Milady, as a matter of fact I have.  My allies and I believe him to be one and the same man as the renegade Tharn.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93I knew it!$94  Barenziah stood up and tried to mask her upheaval.  The Nightingale -- Jagar Tharn!  Oh, but the man was a demon!  Diabolical and insidious.  And so very clever.  He had contrived their downfall seamlessly, perfectly!  Symmachus, my Symmachus...!  <BR>
<BR>
Eadwyre coughed diffidently.  $93Milady, I... we... we need your aid.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah smiled grimly at the irony.  $93I do believe I should be the one saying those words.  But go on, please.  Of what assistance might I be, Milord King?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Quickly the monarch outlined a plot.  The mage Ria Silmane, of late apprenticed to the vile Jagar Tharn, had been killed and declared a traitor by the false Emperor.  Yet she had retained a bit of her powers and could still contact a few of those she had known well on the mortal plane.  She had chosen a Champion who would undertake to find the Staff of Chaos, which had been hidden by the traitorous sorcerer in an unknown site.  This Champion was to wield the Staff's power to destroy Jagar Tharn, who was otherwise invulnerable, and rescue the true Emperor being held prisoner in another dimension.  However, the Champion, while thankfully still alive, now languished in the Imperial Dungeons.  Tharn's attention must be diverted while the chosen one gained freedom with Ria's spirit's help.  Barenziah had the false Emperor's ears -- and seemingly his eyes.  Would she provide the necessary distraction?  <BR>
<BR>
$93I suppose I could obtain another audience with him,$94 Barenziah said carefully.  $93But would that be sufficient?  I must tell you that my children and I have just recently been declared traitors to the Empire.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93In Mournhold, perhaps, Milady, and Morrowind.  Things are different in the Imperial City and the Imperial Province.  The same administrative morass that makes it near impossible to obtain an audience with the Emperor and his ministers also quite assures that you would never be unlawfully imprisoned or otherwise punished without benefit of due legal process.  In your case, Milady, and your children's, the situation is further exacerbated by your royal rank.  As Queen and heirs apparent, your persons are considered inviolable -- sacrosanct, in fact.$94  The King grinned.  $93The Imperial bureaucracy, Milady, is a double-edged claymore.$94  <BR>
<BR>
So.  At least she and the children were safe for the time being.  Then a thought struck her.  $93Milord King, what did you mean earlier when you said I had the false Emperor's eyes?  And seemingly, at that?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Eadwyre looked uncomfortable.  $93It was whispered among the servants that Jagar Tharn kept your likeness in a sort of shrine in his chambers.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93I see.$94  Her thoughts wandered momentarily to that insane romance of hers with the Nightingale.  She had been madly in love with him.  Foolish woman.  And the man she had once loved had caused to be killed the man she truly did love.  Did love.  Loved.  He's gone now, he's... he...  She still couldn't bring herself to accept the fact that Symmachus was dead.  But even if he is, she told herself firmly, my love is alive, and remains.  He would always be with her.  As would the pain.  The pain of living the rest of her life without him.  The pain of trying to survive each day, each night, without his presence, his comfort, his love.  The pain of knowing he would never see his children grow into a fine pair of adults, who would never know their father, how brave he was, how strong, how wonderful, how loving... especially little Morgiah.  <BR>
<BR>
And for that, for all that, for all you have done to my family, Nightingale -- you must die.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Does that surprise you?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Eadwyre's words broke into her thoughts.  $93What?  Does what surprise me?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Your likeness.  In Tharn's room.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Oh.$94  Her features set imperturbably.  $93Yes.  And no.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Eadwyre could see from her expression that she wished to change the subject.  He turned once again to their plans.  $93Our chosen one may need a few days to escape, Milady.  Can you gain him a bit more time?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93You trust me in this, Milord King?  Why?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93We are desperate, Milady.  We have no choice.  But even if we did -- why, yes.  Yes, I would trust you.  I do trust you.  Your husband has been good to my family over the years.  The Lord Symmachus--$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Is dead.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93What?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah related the recent events quickly and coolly.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Milady... Queen... but how dreadful!  I... I'm so sorry...$94  <BR>
<BR>
For the first time Barenziah's glacial poise was shaken.  In the face of sympathy, she felt her outward calm start to crumble.  She gathered her composure, and willed herself to stillness.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Under the circumstances, Milady, we can hardly ask--$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Nay, good Milord.  Under the circumstances I must do what I may to avenge myself upon the murderer of my children's father.$94  A single tear escaped the fortress of her eyes.  She brushed it away impatiently.  $93In return I ask only that you protect my orphaned children as you may.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Eadwyre drew himself up.  His eyes shone.  $93Willingly do I so pledge, most brave and noble Queen.  The gods of our beloved land, indeed Tamriel itself, be my witnesses.$94  <BR>
<BR>
His words touched her absurdly, yet profoundly.  $93I thank you from my heart and my soul, good Milord King Eadwyre.  You have mine and m-my children's e-everlasting g-gra --  grati -- $94  <BR>
<BR>
She broke down.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
She did not sleep that night, but sat in a chair beside her bed, hands folded in her lap, thinking deep and long into the waxing and waning of the darkness.  She would not tell the children -- not yet, not until she must.  <BR>
<BR>
She had no need to seek another audience with the Emperor.  A summons arrived at first light.  <BR>
<BR>
She told the children she expected to be gone a few days, bade them give the servants no trouble, and kissed them good-bye.  Morgiah whimpered a bit; she was bored and lonely in the Imperial City.  Helseth looked dour but said nothing.  He was very like his father.  His father...  <BR>
<BR>
At the Imperial Palace, Barenziah was escorted not into the great audience hall but to a small parlour where the Emperor sat at a solitary breakfast.  He nodded a greeting and waved his hand toward the window.  $93Magnificent view, isn't it?$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah stared out over the towers of the great city.  It dawned on her that this was the very chamber where she'd first met Tiber Septim all those years ago.  Centuries ago.  Tiber Septim.  Another man she had loved.  Who else had she loved?  Symmachus, Tiber Septim... and Straw.  She remembered the big blond stable-boy with sudden and intense affection.  She never realized it till now, but she had loved Straw.  Only she had never let him know.  She had been so young then, those had been carefree days, halcyon days... before everything, before all this... before... him.  Not Symmachus.  The Nightingale.  She was shocked in spite of herself.  The man could still affect her.  Even now.  Even after all that had happened.  A strong wave of inchoate emotion swept over her.  <BR>
<BR>
When she turned back at last, Uriel Septim had vanished -- and the Nightingale sat in his place.  <BR>
<BR>
$93You knew,$94 he said quietly, scanning her face.  $93You knew.  Instantly.  I wanted to surprise you.  You might at least have pretended.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah spread her arms, trying to pacify the maelstrom churning deep inside her.  $93I'm afraid my skill at pretence is no match for yours, my liege.$94  <BR>
<BR>
He sighed.  $93You're angry.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Just a little, I must admit,$94 she said icily.  $93I don't know about you, but I find betrayal a trifle offensive.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93How human of you.$94  <BR>
<BR>
She took a deep breath.  $93What do you want of me?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Now you are pretending.$94  He stood up to face her directly.  $93You know what I want of you.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93You want to torment me.  Go ahead.  I'm in your power.  But leave my children alone.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93No, no, no.  I don't want that at all, Barenziah.$94  He came near, speaking low in the old caressing voice that had sent shivers cascading through her body.  The same voice that was doing the same thing to her, here and now.  $93Don't you see?  This was the only way.$94  His hands closed on her arms.  <BR>
<BR>
She felt her resolve fading, her disgust at him weakening.  $93You could have taken me with you.$94  Unbidden tears gathered in her eyes.  <BR>
<BR>
He shook his head.  $93I didn't have the power.  Ah, but now, now...!  I have it all.  Mine to have, mine to share, mine to give -- to you.$94  He once more waved his hand toward the window and the city beyond.  $93All Tamriel is mine to lay at your feet -- and that is only the beginning.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93It's too late.  Too late.  You left me to him.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93He's dead.  The peasant's dead.  A scant few years -- what do they matter?$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93The children--$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Can be adopted by me.  And we'll have others together, Barenziah.  Oh, and what children they'll be!  What things we shall pass on to them!  Your beauty, and my magic.  I have powers you haven't even dreamt of, not in your most untamed imaginings!$94  He moved to kiss her.  <BR>
<BR>
She slipped his grasp and turned away.  $93I don't believe you.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93You do, you know.  You're still angry, that's all.$94  He smiled.  But it didn't reach his eyes.  $93Tell me what you want, Barenziah.  Barenziah my beloved.  Tell me.  It shall be yours.$94  <BR>
<BR>
Her whole life flashed in front of her.  The past, the present, and the future still to come.  Different times, different lives, different Barenziahs.  Which one was the real one?  Which one was the real Barenziah?  For by that choice she would determine the shape of her fate.  <BR>
<BR>
She made it.  She knew.  She knew who the real Barenziah was, and what she wanted.  <BR>
<BR>
$93A walk in the garden, my liege,$94 she said.  $93A song or two, perhaps.$94  <BR>
<BR>
The Nightingale laughed.  $93You want to be courted.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93And why not?  You do it so well.  It's been long, besides, since I've had the pleasure.$94  <BR>
<BR>
He smiled.  $93As you wish, Milady Queen Barenziah.  Your wish is my command.$94  He took her hand and kissed it.  $93Now, and forever.$94  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
And so they spent their days in courtship -- walking, talking, singing and laughing together, while the Empire's business was left to subordinates.  <BR>
<BR>
$93I'd like to see the Staff,$94 Barenziah said idly one day.  $93I only had a glimpse of it, you'll recall.$94  <BR>
<BR>
He frowned.  $93Nothing would give me greater pleasure, heart's delight -- but that would be impossible.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93You don't trust me,$94 Barenziah pouted, but softened her lips when he leaned over for a kiss.  <BR>
<BR>
$93Nonsense, love.  Of course I do.  But it isn't here.$94  He chuckled.  $93In fact, it isn't anywhere.$94  He kissed her again, more passionately this time.  <BR>
<BR>
$93You're talking in riddles again.  I want to see it.  You couldn't have destroyed it.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Ah.  You've gained in wisdom since last we met.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93You inspired my hunger for knowledge somewhat.$94  She stood up.  $93The Staff of Chaos can't be destroyed.  And it can't be removed from Tamriel, not without the direst consequences to the land itself.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93Ahhh.  You impress me, my love.  All true.  It is not destroyed, and it is not removed from Tamriel.  And yet, as I said, it isn't anywhere.  Can you solve the puzzle?$94  He pulled her to him and she leaned into his embrace.  $93Here's a greater riddle still,$94 he whispered.  $93How does one make one of two?  That I can, and will, show you.$94  Their bodies merged, limbs tangled together.  <BR>
<BR>
Later, when they had drawn a bit apart and he lay dozing, she thought sleepily, $93One of two, two of one, three of two, two of three... what cannot be destroyed or banished might be split apart, perhaps...$94  <BR>
<BR>
She stood up, eyes blazing.  She started to smile.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
The Nightingale kept a journal.  He scribbled entries onto it every night after quick reports from underlings.  It was locked in a bureau.  But the lock was a simple one.  She had, after all, been a member of the Thieves Guild in a past life... in another life... another Barenziah...  <BR>
<BR>
One morning Barenziah managed to sneak a quick look at it while he was occupied at his toilet.  She discovered that the first piece of the Staff of Chaos was hidden in an ancient Dwarvish mine called Fang Lair -- although its location was given only in the vaguest of terms.  The diary was crammed with jotted events in an odd shorthand, and was very hard to decipher.  <BR>
<BR>
All Tamriel, she thought, in his hands and mine, and more perhaps -- and yet...  <BR>
<BR>
For all his exterior charm there was a cold emptiness where his heart should have been, a vacuum of which he was quite unaware, she thought.  One could glimpse it now and then, when his eyes would go blank and hard.  And yet, though he had a different concept of it, he yearned for happiness too, and contentment.  Peasant dreams, Barenziah thought, and Straw flashed before her eyes again, looking lost and sad.  And then Therris, with a feline Khajiit smile.  Tiber Septim, powerful and lonely.  Symmachus, solid, stolid Symmachus, who did what ought to be done, quietly and efficiently.  The Nightingale.  The Nightingale, a riddle and a certainty, both the darkness and the light.  The Nightingale, who would rule all, and more -- and spread chaos in the name of order.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah got reluctant leave from him to visit her children, who had yet to be told of their father's death -- and of the Emperor's offer of protection.  She finally did, and it wasn't easy.  Morgiah clung to her for what seemed an era, sobbing wretchedly, while Helseth ran off into the garden to be alone, afterward refusing all her attempts to speak to him on the subject of his father, or even to let her hold him to her breast.  <BR>
<BR>
Eadwyre called on her while she was there.  She told him what she had discovered so far, explaining that she must remain awhile yet and learn more as she could.  <BR>
<BR>
The Nightingale teased her about her elderly admirer.  He was quite aware of Eadwyre's suspicion -- but he wasn't the least bit perturbed, for no one took the old fool seriously.  Barenziah even managed to arrange a reconciliation of sorts between them.  Eadwyre publicly recanted his misgivings, and his $93old friend$94 the Emperor forgave him.  He was afterward invited to dine with them at least once a week.  <BR>
<BR>
The children liked Eadwyre, even Helseth, who disapproved of his mother's liaison with the Emperor and consequently detested him.  He had become surly and temperamental as the days passed, and frequently quarreled with both his mother and her lover.  Eadwyre was not happy with the affair either, and the Nightingale took great delight at times in openly displaying his affection for Barenziah just to nettle the old man.  <BR>
<BR>
They could not marry, of course, for Uriel Septim was already married.  At least, not yet.  The Nightingale had exiled the Empress shortly after taking the Emperor's place, but had not dared harm her.  She was given sanctuary by the Temple of the One.  It had been given out that she was suffering from ill health, and rumors had been circulated by the Nightingale's agents that she had mental problems.  The Emperor's children had likewise been dispatched to various prisons all across Tamriel disguised as $93schools.$94  <BR>
<BR>
$93She'll grow worse in time,$94 Nightingale said carelessly, referring to the Empress and eyeing Barenziah's swollen breasts and swelling belly with satisfaction.  $93As for their children...  Well, life is full of hazards, isn't it? We'll be married.  Your child will be my true heir.$94  <BR>
<BR>
He did want the child.  Barenziah was sure of that.  She was far less sure, however, of his feelings for her.  They argued continually now, often violently, usually about Helseth, whom he wanted to send away to school in Summurset Isle, the province farthest from the Imperial City.  Barenziah made no effort to avoid these altercations.  The Nightingale, after all, had no interest in a smooth, unruffled life; and besides, he thoroughly enjoyed making up afterward...  <BR>
<BR>
Occasionally Barenziah would take the children and retreat to their old apartment, declaring she wanted no more to do with him.  But he would always come to fetch her back, and she would always let herself be fetched back.  It was ineffable, like the rising and setting of Tamriel's twin moons.  <BR>
<BR>
***<BR>
<BR>
She was six months pregnant before she finally deciphered the location of the last Staff piece -- an easy one, since every Dark Elf knew where the Mount of Dagoth-Ur was.  <BR>
<BR>
When she next quarreled with the Nightingale, she simply left the city with Eadwyre and rode hard for High Rock, and Wayrest.  The Nightingale was furious, but there was little he could do.  His assassins were rather inept, and he dared not leave his seat of power to pursue them in person.  Nor could he openly declare war on Wayrest.  He had no legitimate claim on her or her unborn child.  True to form, the Imperial City's nobility had disapproved of his liaison with Barenziah -- as they had so many years ago of Tiber Septim's -- and were glad to see her go.  <BR>
<BR>
Wayrest was equally distrustful of her, but Eadwyre was fanatically loved by his prosperous little city-state, and allowances were readily made for his... eccentricities.  Barenziah and Eadwyre were married a year after the birth of her son by the Nightingale.  In spite of this unfortunate fact, Eadwyre doted on her and her children.  She in her turn did not love him -- but she was fond of him, and that was something.  It was nice to have someone, and Wayrest was a very good place, a good place for children to grow up, while they waited, and bided their time, and prayed for the Champion's success in his mission.  <BR>
<BR>
Barenziah could only hope that he wouldn't take very long, whoever this unnamed Champion was.  She was a Dark Elf, and she had all the time in the world.  All the time.  But no more love left to give, and no more hatred left to burn.  She had nothing left, nothing but pain, and memories... and her children.  She only wanted to raise her family, and provide them a good life, and be left to live out what remained of hers.  She had no doubt it was going to be a long life yet.  And during it she wanted peace, and quiet, and serenity, of her soul as well as of her heart.  Peasant dreams.  That was what she wanted.  That was what the real Barenziah wanted.  That was what the real Barenziah was.  Peasant dreams.  <BR>
<BR>
Pleasant dreams.  <BR>

"""<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><BR>
